nodes.title: The generic global datum of Breuil–Herzig–Hu–Morra–Schraen
nodes.statement: A generic global datum consists of: a prime p > 5; a totally real field F unramified at every place of the set S_p of places above p; a quaternion algebra D with centre F, split at every place of S_p and at no more than one infinite place (the indefinite case when it is split at exactly one, the definite case when at none), with (F, D) ≠ (ℚ, M₂(ℚ)) in the indefinite case, S_D its set of finite ramified places, a maximal order O_D and fixed isomorphisms (O_D)_w ≅ M₂(O_{F_w}) for w ∉ S_D; a finite field 𝔽 of characteristic p, large enough, with O = W(𝔽); a continuous r̄ : G_F → GL₂(𝔽) such that r̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible, r̄_w = r̄|G_{F_w} is generic (EGS15 Definition 2.1.1) for every w ∈ S_p, and the framed deformation ring of r̄_w over W(𝔽) is formally smooth for every w ∈ (S_D ∪ S_r) ∖ S_p, where S_r is the set of places at which r̄ ramifies (S_p ⊆ S_r by genericity); the character ψ : G_F → W(𝔽)^× that is the Teichmüller lift of ω·det r̄, ω the mod p cyclotomic character; a distinguished place v ∈ S_p, f = [F_v : ℚ_p], such that r̄_v is semisimple and, up to twist, r̄_v|I_{F_v} ≅ ω_f^{Σ_i p^i(r_i+1)} ⊕ 1 with 12 ≤ r_i ≤ p − 15 for all i, or r̄_v|I_{F_v} ≅ ω_{2f}^{Σ_i p^i(r_i+1)} ⊕ ω_{2f}^{p^f Σ_i p^i(r_i+1)} with 13 ≤ r_0 ≤ p − 14 and 12 ≤ r_i ≤ p − 15 for 0 < i < f; an auxiliary finite place w₁ ∉ S_D ∪ S_r with Norm(w₁) ≢ 1 mod p, with the ratio of the eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_{w₁}) outside {1, Norm(w₁), Norm(w₁)^{−1}}, and with w₁ dividing no ζ + ζ^{−1} − 2 for ζ a nontrivial root of unity in a quadratic extension of F; a finite set S of finite places containing S_D ∪ S_r and not w₁, with the framed deformation ring of r̄_w^∨ formally smooth for w ∈ S ∖ S_p; and a compact open U = ∏_w U_w ⊆ ∏_w (O_D)_w^× with U_w = GL₂(O_{F_w}) for w ∉ S ∪ {w₁} and for w ∈ S_p, U_{w₁} contained in the matrices that are upper triangular and unipotent modulo w₁, and such that r̄ is modular at the level V = ∏_{w ∉ S_D ∪ S_r}(O_D)_w^× · ∏_{w ∈ (S_D ∪ S_r)∖S_p} U_w · ∏_{w ∈ S_p}(1 + pM₂(O_{F_w})): Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹_ét(X_V ×_F F̄, 𝔽)) ≠ 0 in the indefinite case, S(V, 𝔽)[𝔪] ≠ 0 in the definite case.
hypotheses: The genericity bounds at v force p > 23 (BHHMS, remark after the genericity conditions, p. 5); in fact 12 ≤ p − 15 needs p ≥ 27, so p ≥ 29 since p is prime (arithmetic derived here, not stated in BHHMS).
Hodge–Tate weights are normalized so that the p-adic cyclotomic character ε has weight 1 at every embedding; Frobenius elements are geometric (BHHMS §1.4 and §8.1).
r̄_v^∨ satisfies the same semisimplicity and genericity hypotheses as r̄_v (BHHMS §8.1 (i)); this is used because the patched rings are rings for r̄_v^∨.
proofSteps: Record the data and conditions of BHHMS §8.1, items (i)–(iv) together with the standing assumptions on F, D, r̄ and ψ (pp. 86–87); the genericity conditions of the introduction, (i)–(iii) on p. 5, are the same conditions in another order.

The auxiliary place w₁ exists by Chebotarev (EGS15 §6.2, citing Lemma 4.11 of Darmon–Diamond–Taylor; BHHMS cite EGS15 §§6.2 and 6.5); the conditions on w₁ make the level U sufficiently small in the sense of Kisin (2.1.2) (EGS15 §6.2).
The shape of V in the modularity hypothesis is always available once r̄ is modular at some level (BHHMS §8.1, citing Breuil–Diamond Theorem 3.2.2 and the proof of Corollary 3.2.3).

nodes.title: The Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis set of Serre weights
nodes.statement: Let K/ℚ_p be unramified of degree f with residue field k, embeddings κ_j = κ_0 ∘ φ^j : k → 𝔽, and let ρ : G_K → GL₂(𝔽) be continuous. A Serre weight is an irreducible 𝔽-representation σ_{t,s} = ⊗_{j=0}^{f−1}(det^{t_j} Sym^{s_j} k²) ⊗_{k, κ_j} 𝔽 of GL₂(k), 0 ≤ s_j, t_j ≤ p − 1, not all t_j equal to p − 1. The set W(ρ) of Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis is a set of Serre weights depending only on ρ, with W(ρ) ⊆ W(ρ^ss). For semisimple reducible ρ, σ_{t,s} ∈ W(ρ) if and only if there is J ⊆ {0, …, f − 1} with ρ|I_K ≅ ω_f^{Σ_j t_j p^j} ⊗ (ω_f^{Σ_{j∈J}(s_j+1)p^j} ⊕ ω_f^{Σ_{j∉J}(s_j+1)p^j}); for irreducible ρ, σ_{t,s} ∈ W(ρ) if and only if there is J ⊆ {0, …, 2f − 1}, antisymmetric in the sense that i ∈ J exactly when i + f ∉ J (indices modulo 2f, s_j extended f-periodically), with ρ|I_K ≅ ω_f^{Σ_j t_j p^j} ⊗ (ω_{2f}^{Σ_{j∈J}(s_j+1)p^j} ⊕ ω_{2f}^{Σ_{j∉J}(s_j+1)p^j}). For a nonsplit reducible ρ, W(ρ) is the subset of W(ρ^ss) of those weights for which the extension class of ρ lies in the subspace L_α ⊆ H¹(G_K, 𝔽(χ₁χ₂^{−1})) attached by BDJ10 §3.2 to the weight and its subset J: the classes that are reductions of crystalline extensions with the associated labelled Hodge–Tate weights, enlarged to all of H¹ when χ₁χ₂^{−1} is cyclotomic, b = (p, …, p) and J is everything, and by the unramified classes when χ₁χ₂^{−1} is trivial and J is not everything. The displayed descriptions use BDJ10 §3 and BHHMS §2.3: ω_f is the character I_K → O_K^× → k^× → 𝔽^× induced by inverse geometric Artin reciprocity, with ω₁ equal to the mod p cyclotomic character. EGS15 uses the inverse fundamental characters; with the same Galois representation as input its set D is related by W(ρ) = D_EGS(ρ^∨), not by W(ρ) = D_EGS(ρ).
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p unramified; for ramified K the Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis recipe is replaced by the generalisations of Schein and Gee, which are not needed here.

Use the BDJ/BHHMS fundamental characters throughout. EGS15 §2 has κ_{j+1}^p = κ_j and writes weights using κ_{−j}; hence its weight embeddings κ_{−j} agree with our κ₀ ∘ φ^j. Its ω_f is our ω_f^{−1}, so comparison with its formula requires dualising the input Galois representation.
BHHMS use W(r̄_w^∨), the weight set of the dual representation, because their patched rings are deformation rings of r̄_w^∨ (BHHMS §8.1, (61)).
proofSteps: Use BDJ10 §3.1–3.2 directly for the semisimple recipes, including the antisymmetric subset condition, and for W(ρ) ⊆ W(ρ^ss). Translate EGS15 §2 by both its embedding convention and its inverse fundamental characters: W(ρ) = D_EGS(ρ^∨).

For the nonsplit reducible case the subset condition is BDJ10's L_J condition, phrased through crystalline lifts with prescribed labelled Hodge–Tate weights (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3 supplies the crystalline lifting rings and their points).

When ρ is tame and its inertial parameter is 1-deep, the description agrees with the parametrisation of MP.3/tame-weight-set by the extension-graph labels; prove agreement by matching the subset J with the sign vector of MP.3.

nodes.title: Quaternionic spaces of mod p forms and their residual eigenspaces
nodes.statement: Fix a generic global datum and a compact open V = ∏_w V_w ⊆ U with V_w = (O_D)_w^× outside S ∪ {w₁}. For a continuous representation σ of K_S = ∏_{w∈S} V_w on a finite O-module with a central character compatible with ψ, let σ(θ) be its twist by the square roots θ_w of the central characters (p > 2), and extend the action to V·(𝔸_F^∞)^× by letting (𝔸_F^∞)^× act through (𝔸_F^∞)^×/F^× → G_F^{ab} → O^× composed with ψ^{−1}. In the indefinite case let X_V be the smooth projective Shimura curve over F (sign convention of BDJ10), replaced by its quotient by the free action of the finite group V(𝔸_F^∞)^×/VF^×, and S(σ) = H¹(X_V ×_F F̄, F_{σ(θ)^*}); in the definite case S(σ) is the space of functions f : D^×∖(D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^× → σ(θ)^* with f(gu) = u^{−1}f(g) for u ∈ V(𝔸_F^∞)^×. The algebra T^{S,univ} = O[T_w, S_w : w ∉ S ∪ {w₁}] acts through the double cosets of diag(ϖ_w, 1) and diag(ϖ_w, ϖ_w); 𝔪 is the maximal ideal generated by T_w − S_w tr r̄(Frob_w) and Norm(w) − S_w det r̄(Frob_w). Then σ ↦ S(σ)_𝔪 is contravariantly exact; in the indefinite case the evaluation map Hom_{T(σ)_𝔪[G_{F,S}]}(ρ(σ)_𝔪, S(σ)_𝔪) ⊗_{T(σ)_𝔪} ρ(σ)_𝔪 → S(σ)_𝔪 is an isomorphism, where ρ(σ)_𝔪 : G_{F,S} → GL₂(T(σ)_𝔪) is induced from the universal deformation; and M(σ) is the Pontryagin dual of Hom_{T(σ)_𝔪[G_{F,S}]}(ρ(σ)_𝔪, S(σ)_𝔪) (indefinite) or of S(σ)_𝔪 (definite). The resulting σ ↦ M(σ) is covariantly exact. For σ = 𝔽 trivial, when its central character is compatible, the r̄-part Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹_ét(X_V ×_F F̄, 𝔽)) is unchanged by the passage to the quotient curve.
hypotheses: V sufficiently small in the sense of Kisin (2.1.2), guaranteed by the choice of V_{w₁}; 𝔪 non-Eisenstein because r̄ is absolutely irreducible.
The action of (𝔸_F^∞)^× is through ψ^{−1}, not ψ: BHHMS Remark 8.1.3(i) corrects EGS15 §6.2 here (recorded as a source finding).

In the indefinite case the curve is replaced by its quotient by the finite group of central elements (BHHMS Remark 8.1.3(iii)); this is needed for S(σ) to be well defined with the extended central action.

In the definite case D may ramify at finite places (any F with [F:ℚ] + |S_D| even); the parent R18.3 plans the definite class sets only in the Khare–Wintenberger setting, and the general case is requested from it.
proofSteps: Construct S(σ) on the HMV R18.4 finite-level cohomology with the R18.4 algebraic local systems (indefinite) and on the R18.3 definite class set with its fixed-central-character forms (definite).
The Hecke operators T_w, S_w are the R18.4 correspondences; 𝔪 is the R18.3 residual Hecke ideal in the normalisation of BDJ10 §4 (BHHMS Remark 8.1.3(ii)).

Local systems: a finite σ factoring through K_S/V′ for V′ ⊆ V open normal gives a local system by descent of the constant sheaf along the finite Galois cover X_{V′} → X_V, the same torsor construction as R18.4/quaternion-local-systems for algebraic coefficients.

Exactness: localisation at the non-Eisenstein 𝔪 kills H⁰ and H² of every finite coefficient system (R18.4/residual-eisenstein-vanishing over 𝔽, by dévissage for finite length coefficients), so the long exact sequences give contravariant exactness of σ ↦ S(σ)_𝔪, since the coefficient system uses σ^*; the additional dual in M restores covariance; taking ψ-parts is exact by R18.4/central-character-exactness.

The Galois representation ρ(σ)_𝔪 comes from R18.4/early-quaternionic-galois-hecke-support (constant weight-two coefficients) through the map from the universal deformation ring: for σ trivial on V′, T(σ)_𝔪 is a quotient of the Hecke algebra acting on constant-coefficient cohomology at level V′; the evaluation isomorphism is the Eichler–Shimura/Boston–Lenstra–Ribet statement cited by EGS15 §6.2 (Carayol, Théorème 4).

Quotient curve: the finite group acts freely (R18.1/quaternionic-effective-stabilizers), the quotient is a smooth projective curve over F, and Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹) does not change (BHHMS Remark 8.1.3(iii), arguing as in Breuil–Diamond Theorem 3.7.1).

Three corrections to EGS15 §6.2: the adelic centre acts through ψ^{−1}; the maximal ideal is the one of BDJ10 §4; the Shimura curve is replaced by its quotient by a finite group acting freely, which does not change the r̄-part.

nodes.title: Projectivity and injectivity of the residual eigenspaces over the level quotient
nodes.statement: Let V′ ⊆ V be compact open subgroups of (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^×, V′ normal in V, with V sufficiently small in the sense of Kisin (2.1.2) (for example V_{w₁} unipotent upper triangular modulo w₁), so that G = V/V′ (modulo the central part, as in GK.0/residual-eigenspaces) acts freely on the quotient curve X_{V′}, respectively on D^×∖(D ⊗ 𝔸_F^∞)^×/V′(𝔸_F^∞)^×. Then H¹_ét(X_{V′} ×_F F̄, 𝔽)_𝔪 (indefinite) and S(V′, 𝔽)_𝔪 (definite) are finite projective 𝔽[G]-modules, hence injective; for every finite 𝔽[V]-representation σ factoring through G, the Hochschild–Serre map identifies the 𝔪-localised cohomology at level V with coefficients in σ^∗ with Hom_G(σ, H¹_ét(X_{V′} ×_F F̄, 𝔽)_𝔪) (resp. Hom_G(σ, S(V′, 𝔽)_𝔪)), compatibly with the Hecke operators away from S ∪ {w₁} and with G_F. The same holds with W(𝔽)/pⁿ coefficients, with projectivity and injectivity over (W(𝔽)/pⁿ)[G]. When G is a p-group these projective modules are free, since the group algebra is local; this includes the Taylor–Wiles quotients and the pro-p congruence quotients used below.
hypotheses: 𝔪 is non-Eisenstein because r̄ is absolutely irreducible; the free action of G at small level is the condition imposed by the auxiliary place w₁ (EGS15 §6.2; BHHMS Remark 8.1.3(iii), citing Breuil–Diamond Lemme 3.6.2).
proofSteps: Indefinite case: X_{V′} → X_V is a finite étale Galois cover with group G, so RΓ(X_{V′}, 𝔽) ≅ RΓ(X_V, 𝔽[G]) is a perfect complex of 𝔽[G]-modules computed by the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence of R18.4/finite-level-descent (the case where p divides |G|).

After localisation at 𝔪, H⁰ and H² vanish (R18.4/residual-eisenstein-vanishing). The remaining finite module has finite projective dimension over 𝔽[G]. The finite group algebra is self-injective, so finite projective dimension forces projectivity and hence injectivity. For W(𝔽)/pⁿ the same argument uses its Frobenius group algebra and the corresponding perfect coefficient complex. Projective implies free when G is a p-group, not for an arbitrary finite G.
The Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for coefficients σ therefore degenerates and gives the Hom description; Hecke operators and G_F commute with the comparison maps.

Definite case: S(V′, 𝔽) is the space of functions on a finite set on which G acts freely, so it is free over 𝔽[G] before localisation; the 𝔪-part is a direct summand (as in R18.3/tw-freeness, which is the Taylor–Wiles instance of this statement). A direct summand is projective; no assertion that it is free for arbitrary G is needed.

sources.locator: proof of Corollary 8.4.6, part (i), p. 107; (64), p. 89

Because the level is sufficiently small and 𝔪 is non-Eisenstein, σ ↦ S(σ)_𝔪 is exact.

acceptance: Projectivity and injectivity hold for arbitrary finite level quotients; freeness is asserted only for p-group quotients. For odd p, the one-dimensional trivial summand of 𝔽[C₂] is projective but not free, so replacing projective by free in the general statement fails a dimension check.
The level must be small enough for G to act freely; this is where the auxiliary place w₁ enters.

nodes.title: Mod p cohomology of Shimura curves at infinite level at v
nodes.statement: Fix a generic global datum and Serre weights σ_w ∈ W(r̄_w^∨) for w ∈ S_p ∖ {v}, and a tame level V^v = ∏_{w≠v} V_w with V_w = U_w for w ∉ S_p and V_w ⊆ 1 + pM₂(O_{F_w}) normal in GL₂(O_{F_w}) for w ∈ S_p ∖ {v}. Define the smooth representation π of GL₂(F_v) over 𝔽 as the colimit over compact open V_v ⊆ GL₂(F_v) of Hom_{U^v/V^v}(⊗_{w∈S_p∖{v}} σ_w, Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹_ét(X_{V^vV_v} ×_F F̄, 𝔽))) in the indefinite case, and of Hom_{U^v/V^v}(⊗_w σ_w, S(V^vV_v, 𝔽)[𝔪]) in the definite case; GL₂(F_v) acts through the Hecke action of g ∈ GL₂(F_v) between the levels V_v and gV_vg^{−1}. Then π is admissible, has central character ψ^{−1} (on F_v^× through local class field theory), and π ≠ 0. The unweighted variant π(V^v) = colim_{V_v} Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹_ét(X_{V^vV_v} ×_F F̄, 𝔽)) (definite: colim S(V^vV_v, 𝔽)[𝔪]) is admissible smooth for every tame level V^v; when V_{w₁} consists of the matrices upper triangular and unipotent modulo w₁, V_w = U_w at the other places outside S_p, and V_w ⊆ 1 + pM₂(O_{F_w}) is normal in GL₂(O_{F_w}) at w ∈ S_p ∖ {v}, it has a finite filtration whose graded pieces are subrepresentations of weighted π's, at least one of them nonzero if π(V^v) ≠ 0 (BHHMS (83)).
hypotheses: Admissibility: for every compact open V_v the invariants π^{V_v} are finite-dimensional, being contained in the r̄-part of a finite-level cohomology group (non-Eisenstein localisation makes the comparison with finite level exact).
The σ_w are taken in W(r̄_w^∨) so that π ≠ 0 by the weight theorem; for other weights the corresponding space vanishes.
proofSteps: The colimit is the fixed-exponent smooth colimit of CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.1, applied to the quaternionic Shimura-curve tower (CC.8/arithmetic-tower-realisation, in its quaternionic form as used by CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.1/shimura-curve-completed-cohomology; in the definite case the tower is a system of finite sets) with the level varying at v only, which is cofinal in the levels at v; smoothness and the GL₂(F_v)-action are CC.1/full-local-group-smooth-action, and the Hecke operators away from S ∪ {w₁} are CC.1/tame-hecke-on-colimits for this tower, with the ψ^{−1} central twist.
Admissibility: by GK.0/non-eisenstein-freeness the V_v-invariants of the colimit agree with the finite-level r̄-part at level V^vV_v for V_v small, which is finite-dimensional.
Central character: the centre acts through ψ^{−1} because of the twisted central action in the definition of the spaces (GK.0/residual-eigenspaces).
Nonvanishing: GK.0/bdj-weight-theorem with σ_w ∈ W(r̄_w^∨) and the existence of some weight σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨).

Dévissage (BHHMS (83)), for the shrunken levels only: write the maximal central-character quotient of Ind_{V_w}^{GL₂(O_{F_w})} 1 as an iterated extension of Serre weights; injectivity of the localized H¹ as a U^v/V^v-representation (GK.0/non-eisenstein-freeness) lets one bound π(V^v) by the weighted pieces.

sources.match: The admissible smooth representation π of GL₂(F_v): the colimit over levels at v of the r̄-part of H¹ of Shimura curves (or of the 𝔪-torsion of definite forms), possibly weighted by fixed Serre weights at the other places above p, with central character ψ^{−1}; the unweighted version reduces to weighted ones by dévissage.
The global representation π_glob as a colimit of r̄-parts of mod p cohomology of quaternionic Shimura curves (or definite forms) over levels at v, with commuting Hecke and Galois actions.

acceptance: The colimit is over levels at v only; the levels away from v are fixed.
The weighted π uses Hom_{U^v/V^v}(⊗σ_w, −), not a tensor product.

nodes.title: The weight part of Serre's conjecture for quaternion algebras (Gee–Kisin)
nodes.statement: Let p > 2, F totally real, r̄ : G_F → GL₂(𝔽) modular with r̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} irreducible (and, for p = 5, projective image of r̄|G_{F(ζ_5)} not A₅), and D a quaternion algebra over F split above p and at no more than one infinite place, compatible with r̄ at its finite ramified places. For Serre weights σ_w of GL₂(k_w), w | p, r̄ is modular for D of weight ⊗_w σ_w if and only if σ_w ∈ W^{BT}(r̄|G_{F_w}) for all w | p, where W^{BT} is the set of weights with nonzero Breuil–Mézard multiplicity. When p is unramified in F, W^{BT}(ρ) is the Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis set. Here ψ is a fixed character with det r̄ = ψε^{−1} modulo p, the weights are compatible with ψ, and r̄ is modular for D of weight σ if the 𝔪-part of the space of forms of weight σ is nonzero at some level (GK14 Definitions 5.5.2–5.5.3). In the setting of a generic global datum (BHHMS normalisations, which dualise r̄): for V with V_w ⊆ 1 + pM₂(O_{F_w}) normal at w ∈ S_p and such that r̄ is modular at level V (BHHMS (60)), Hom_{GL₂(O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)}(⊗_{w∈S_p}σ_w, Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹_ét(X_V ×_F F̄, 𝔽))) ≠ 0 if and only if σ_w ∈ W(r̄_w^∨) for every w ∈ S_p, and in the definite case the same holds with S(V, 𝔽)[𝔪] in place of the r̄-part of H¹.
hypotheses: p > 2 and, for p = 5, the A₅ exception excluded; both hold for a generic global datum (BHHMS: p > 23).

The identification W^{BT} = W^{BDJ} for p unramified rests on Gee–Liu–Savitt and Gee–Kisin Theorem A(1); it is a recorded gap of this roadmap (no atlas roadmap plans the Breuil–Mézard conjecture for potentially Barsotti–Tate representations).
proofSteps: Patching (GK14 §5.4): for each potentially Barsotti–Tate type, patch the spaces of quaternionic forms with that type at p (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5) and compare the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity of the patched module modulo ϖ (R03.3/degree-indexed-multiplicity) with the Breuil–Mézard multiplicity of the potentially Barsotti–Tate deformation ring; filtering the type lattice modulo ϖ by Serre weights gives one inequality (the analogue for general totally real F of GL2ModularityLifting R32.2/patched-weight-filtration, which is stated only for p totally split) and the Breuil–Mézard identity (GK14 Theorem A, the recorded gap) the other.

Deduce (GK14 Corollary 5.4.5) that the patched module of a Serre weight σ is nonzero exactly when its Breuil–Mézard multiplicity is nonzero, using potential diagonalisability of potentially Barsotti–Tate lifts (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.1) to see that r̄ is modular of some type.

Translate into the original BDJ formulation (GK14 Corollary 5.5.4): Shapiro-type identity (5.5.5) between forms of type τ^p and forms of weight σ at smaller level, and the compatibility of r̄ with D at the ramified places.
For BHHMS's normalisation: the space Hom(⊗σ_w, Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹)) corresponds to the 𝔪-part of forms of weight ⊗σ_w^∨ twisted by ψ; this replaces W(r̄_w) by W(r̄_w^∨) (BHHMS (61), citing GK14 §5.5).

sources.locator: Theorem B (= Corollary 5.5.7), p. 3 and p. 35; Corollary 5.5.4 with Definitions 5.5.2–5.5.3, p. 34; Corollary 5.4.5, p. 33
sources.match: Modularity of a given Serre weight for a quaternion algebra holds exactly when each local weight lies in the Breuil–Mézard weight set and r̄ is compatible with D; for p unramified this is the conjecture of Buzzard, Diamond and Jarvis.
Nonvanishing of the weighted r̄-part of H¹ of Shimura curves at level V is equivalent to σ_w ∈ W(r̄_w^∨) for all w above p, citing Gee–Kisin §5.5.

The support condition for Serre weights of the patching functor follows from Gee–Kisin, cited as Corollaries 5.6.4 and 4.5.7 of the 2012 version (numbering absent from arXiv v5, recorded as a source finding).

acceptance: Stated with W(r̄_w^∨) in BHHMS's normalisation and with the compatibility condition with D implicit in a generic global datum.
The dependence on Gee–Kisin Theorem A is recorded as a gap, not hidden.

nodes.title: Doubling at the auxiliary place w₁
nodes.statement: Let V^v = ∏_{w≠v}V_w be a tame level with V_{w₁} = GL₂(O_{F_{w₁}}) (r̄ unramified at w₁), and let V′^v agree with V^v except that V′_{w₁} is the group of matrices upper triangular and unipotent modulo w₁. Then for every sufficiently small V_v there is an isomorphism Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹_ét(X_{V^vV_v} ×_F F̄, 𝔽))^{⊕2} ≅ Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹_ét(X_{V′^vV_v} ×_F F̄, 𝔽)), and hence a GL₂(F_v)-equivariant isomorphism π(V^v)^{⊕2} ≅ π(V′^v). BHHMS prove the indefinite case and state that the definite case (with S(−, 𝔽)[𝔪]) is similar; the compatibility of the finite-level isomorphisms with change of V_v, which gives the equivariance of the colimit, is part of the argument below.
hypotheses: The three conditions on w₁ of the generic global datum: Norm(w₁) ≢ 1 mod p, eigenvalue ratio of r̄(Frob_{w₁}) outside {1, Norm(w₁)^{±1}}, and the root-of-unity condition.
proofSteps: Since Norm(w₁) ≢ 1 mod p, the torus quotient (k_{w₁}^×)² of the Iwahori level by V′_{w₁} has order prime to p, so the cohomology at level V′ splits into isotypic parts for its characters; an eigenform in a part with a nontrivial character is a ramified principal series at w₁, and by local–global compatibility away from p (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.4) its Galois representation is ramified at w₁ through a character of order prime to p, which stays nontrivial modulo p; as r̄ is unramified at w₁, only the trivial character contributes to the r̄-part, and V′_{w₁}-level equals Iwahori level after taking r̄-parts (work with the integral, 𝔪-localised, O-free cohomology of R18.4/non-eisenstein-integral-control and its eigenspace decomposition R18.4/cohomological-eigenspaces).

At Iwahori level the two degeneracy maps (HMV R18.4/cohomological-degeneracy) give δ from two copies of the hyperspecial level to Iwahori level, with δ†δ the Gram operator (R18.4/geometric-gram-identity, R18.4/degeneracy-gram). On the 𝔪-part at hyperspecial level, T_{w₁} and S_{w₁} act through the Eichler–Shimura relation for r̄(Frob_{w₁}), whose eigenvalues α, β are distinct, so the Gram determinant becomes Δ = (Norm(w₁) − α/β)(Norm(w₁) − β/α), a unit by the eigenvalue condition; hence δ is injective with image a direct summand (R18.4/oldspace-splitting).

There is no new part after localisation: an eigenform new at w₁ is special at w₁; transferring it to GL₂ by the Jacquet–Langlands bridge (HMV R18.4/quaternionic-jacquet-langlands-bridge), local–global compatibility (R19.4, Carayol) shows that the eigenvalue ratio of its residual Frobenius would be Norm(w₁)^{±1}, which is excluded; comparing ranks in characteristic zero and using the direct-summand property gives an isomorphism integrally, hence modulo p.

The isomorphisms are induced by correspondences at w₁ only, so they commute with change of V_v and with the GL₂(F_v)-action, and pass to the colimit (BHHMS proof of Corollary 8.4.6 (ii)). The definite case uses R18.3/definite-degeneracy in place of the cohomological degeneracy maps.

sources.match: By Ihara's lemma at w₁, easy under the assumptions on w₁, two copies of the r̄-part at maximal level at w₁ give the r̄-part at the level of matrices upper triangular unipotent modulo w₁, for V_v small; hence π^{⊕2} ≅ π′.
The three conditions on the auxiliary place w₁ and the level at w₁ consisting of matrices upper triangular and unipotent modulo w₁.

acceptance: The determinant of the degeneracy Gram matrix modulo 𝔪 factors as (N − α/β)(N − β/α) with N = Norm(w₁), and is a unit exactly under the eigenvalue condition.
The statement is used only to compare GK dimensions: dim π(V^v) = dim π(V′^v).

nodes.title: Cancellation of a power-series variable (Hamann)
nodes.statement: If R and S are commutative local rings and R⟦x⟧ ≅ S⟦x⟧ as rings, then R ≅ S. In the complete regular case used here, if A is a complete Noetherian local W(𝔽)-algebra with residue field 𝔽 and A⟦x⟧ ≅ W(𝔽)⟦X₁, …, X_n⟧ as W(𝔽)-algebras, with n ≥ 1, then A ≅ W(𝔽)⟦X₁, …, X_{n−1}⟧. If instead A⟦x⟧ ≅ B⟦x⟧ with B ≅ W(𝔽)⟦X₁, …, X_n⟧, cancellation gives A ≅ B with n variables.
hypotheses: The general statement is Hamann's theorem for local rings; every application in this roadmap is the complete regular case, which has the elementary proof below.
proofSteps: (The second form in the statement is derived here, not stated in BHHMS.) Complete regular case: A⟦x⟧ ≅ W(𝔽)⟦X₁, …, X_n⟧ is regular local and x lies in its maximal ideal but not in its square, so A = A⟦x⟧/(x) is regular local of dimension n (the quotient of a regular local ring by an element of a regular system of parameters).

A is complete with residue field 𝔽 and p ∉ 𝔪_A² (because p ∉ 𝔪² in A⟦x⟧ ≅ W(𝔽)⟦X⟧ and 𝔪_A² ⊆ 𝔪_{A⟦x⟧}²); Cohen's structure theorem gives a surjection W(𝔽)⟦X₁, …, X_{n−1}⟧ ↠ A, which is an isomorphism because both are domains of dimension n (a surjection between Noetherian local domains of the same dimension has zero kernel).
General local rings: Hamann, On power-invariance, Theorem 4.

sources.match: For local rings R, S, an isomorphism of power series rings in one variable over R and over S implies R ≅ S; attributed to Hamann, Theorem 4.
Power-invariance of local rings, as recorded in BHHMS Lemma 8.1.2.

acceptance: Used only to pass between deformation rings with and without one extra formal variable (fixed versus unfixed determinant, GK14 Remark 5.2.2).
The Lean statement takes an arbitrary ring isomorphism of power series rings, not one over a fixed base.

nodes.title: The patched local deformation ring R∞
nodes.statement: For a generic global datum and integers q ≥ [F : ℚ], put R^loc = (⊗̂_{w∈S∖S_p} R_{r̄_w}^{ψ_w}) ⊗̂ (⊗̂_{w∈S_p∖{v}} R_{r̄_w}^{(0,−1),τ_w,ψ_w}) ⊗̂ R_{r̄_v}^{ψ_v} over W(𝔽), where R^{ψ_w} is the framed deformation ring of r̄_w with determinant ε^{−1}ψ_w and R^{(0,−1),τ_w,ψ_w} its reduced p-torsion-free quotient of parallel Hodge–Tate weights (0, −1) and inertial type τ_w; R∞ = R^loc⟦X₁, …, X_{q−[F:ℚ]+|S|−1}⟧ and S∞ = W(𝔽)⟦x₁, …, x_{4|S|+q−1}⟧ with a local W(𝔽)-algebra map S∞ → R∞. Then R_{r̄_w}^{ψ_w} ≅ W(𝔽)⟦X₁, X₂, X₃⟧ for w ∈ S ∖ S_p, R_{r̄_v}^{ψ_v} ≅ W(𝔽)⟦X₁, …, X_{3+3f}⟧, R_{r̄_w}^{(0,−1),τ_w,ψ_w} ≅ R_{r̄_w^∨}^{(1,0),τ_w^∨,ψ_w^{−1}} ≅ W(𝔽)⟦X₁, …, X_{3+[F_w:ℚ_p]}⟧ for w ∈ S_p ∖ {v}, and consequently R∞ ≅ R_{r̄_v}^{ψ_v}⟦X₁, …, X_{4(|S|−1)+q−f}⟧ ≅ W(𝔽)⟦X₁, …, X_{4|S|+q−1+2f}⟧; in particular dim R∞ − dim S∞ = 2f.
hypotheses: For a fixed Hodge and inertial type, the unfixed-determinant lifting ring is the fixed-determinant ring with one unramified determinant variable (GK14 Remark 5.2.2). The analogous one-variable assertion is not made for the unrestricted local deformation ring at v, where determinant characters have ramified directions as well.

Formal smoothness of R_{r̄_w}^{ψ_w} for w ∈ S ∖ S_p is a hypothesis of the datum; for R_{r̄_v}^{ψ_v} BHHMS deduce it from genericity of r̄_v (the reason, supplied here, is that H²(G_{F_v}, ad⁰ r̄_v) vanishes by local duality).
The structure of the potentially Barsotti–Tate rings at w ∈ S_p ∖ {v} is EGS15 Theorem 7.2.1(2), a recorded gap owned by the pending design LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartII (issue #3432).
proofSteps: Build R^loc and R∞ as completed tensor products and power series rings of the local lifting rings of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 with fixed determinant (R08.1/local-fixed-determinant).
Away from p: formal smoothness of the unfixed ring gives W(𝔽)⟦X₁, …, X₄⟧; fixing the determinant and cancelling one variable gives three variables.

At v: genericity gives H²(G_{F_v}, ad⁰ r̄_v) = 0 by local duality (ad⁰ r̄_v has no ω-twist of the trivial character as a quotient), so the fixed-determinant ring is formally smooth of relative dimension 3 + 3f (R08.1/local-tangent-obstruction).

At w ∈ S_p ∖ {v}: duality of Galois representations identifies the (0, −1) ring of r̄_w with the (1, 0) ring of r̄_w^∨, which is a power series ring in 3 + [F_w : ℚ_p] variables (EGS15 Theorem 7.2.1(2), the gap).

Count: Σ_{w∈S_p} [F_w : ℚ_p] = [F : ℚ] since p is unramified in F, so the number of variables over R_{r̄_v}^{ψ_v} is 3|S∖S_p| + Σ_{w∈S_p∖{v}}(3 + [F_w:ℚ_p]) + q − [F:ℚ] + |S| − 1 = 4(|S| − 1) + q − f, and adding 3 + 3f gives 4|S| + q − 1 + 2f.

sources.locator: §8.1, (63) and the paragraph before it, pp. 88–89
sources.match: The local ring R^loc, the patched ring R∞ as a power series ring over it in q − [F:ℚ] + |S| − 1 variables, the formal smoothness of the factors, and the resulting presentation of R∞ as a power series ring over W(𝔽) in 4|S| + q − 1 + 2[F_v:ℚ_p] variables.

The patching data: integers g, q, the ring S∞ in 4#S + q − 1 variables, R∞ a power series ring over the local ring and the map S∞ → R∞.

The potentially Barsotti–Tate rings at w ∈ S_p ∖ {v} are taken from the gap owner, not reproved.

nodes.title: Type and Hodge–Tate quotients of the patched ring
nodes.statement: For a tame inertial type τ of I_{F_v} and λ = ((a_j, b_j))_{0≤j<f} with a_j > b_j, let R_{r̄_v^∨}^{λ,τ} be the reduced p-torsion-free quotient of the framed ring R_{r̄_v^∨} whose Q̄_p-points are the potentially crystalline lifts of r̄_v^∨ of inertial type τ and labelled Hodge–Tate weights (a_j, b_j) at the embedding σ_j; put R∞^{λ,τ} = R∞ ⊗_{R_{r̄_v^∨}} R_{r̄_v^∨}^{λ,τ}, p_{λ,τ} = ker(R∞ ↠ R∞^{λ,τ}), R̄∞^{λ,τ} = R∞^{λ,τ}/(p), and write R∞^{(a,b),τ} when λ_j = (a, b) for all j. Because of the fixed determinant, R∞^{λ,τ} ≠ 0 forces a_j + b_j = 1 for all j; the cases used are λ_j ∈ {(1, 0), (2, −1)}, and after twisting by ε, λ_j ∈ {(2, 1), (3, 0)}.
hypotheses: τ tame; R∞ is the patched ring of GK.1/patched-deformation-ring (whose local factor at v is a ring for r̄_v^∨ under the duality used there).
The domain property of R∞^{λ,τ} for the relevant λ, τ and the reducedness of R̄∞^{(2,−1)_j,τ} come from the gap owned by LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartII (BHHMS Proposition 4.2.1, Corollary 4.2.6).
proofSteps: Define R_{r̄_v^∨}^{λ,τ} as Kisin's potentially crystalline quotient of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3/pst-deformation-ring with the p-adic Hodge type given by λ and Galois type τ (R08.3/hodge-and-galois-types), after twisting by a power of ε so that the weights lie in [0, h] as R08.3 requires (for example (2, −1) becomes (3, 0)), and base change along R_{r̄_v^∨} → R∞.

The nonvanishing condition a_j + b_j = 1: points of the fixed-determinant ring of r̄_v^∨ have determinant εψ_v^{−1} (the dual of ε^{−1}ψ_v), of labelled Hodge–Tate weight 1 at every embedding, and the labelled weight of the determinant at σ_j is a_j + b_j.
Twisting all lifts by ε shifts every weight by (1, 1), identifying the (1,0)/(2,−1) rings with the (2,1)/(3,0) rings and changing determinants to ε³ψ_v^{−1} (BHHMS proof of Theorem 8.3.9).

nodes.title: Fixed-determinant patching functors
nodes.statement: Let K = GL₂(O_{F_v}) (more generally a product of compact open subgroups of GL₂ or of units of quaternion division algebras at finitely many places), R∞ = R⟦x₁, …, x_h⟧ over a completed tensor product R of framed local deformation rings, and C_Z′ a Serre subcategory of the category of continuous representations of K on finitely generated O-modules with central character lifting (ε det ρ̄)|_I ∘ Art. A fixed-determinant patching functor is a covariant exact functor M∞ from C_Z′ to finitely generated R∞-modules (coherent sheaves on Spf R∞) such that: (1) for every σ, M∞(σ) is supported on the fixed-determinant locus X∞^{ψ_σ}; (2) for every K-stable O-lattice σ°(τ) in σ(τ) for an inertial type τ, M∞(σ°(τ)) is p-torsion free, supported on R∞^{ψ,τ} and maximal Cohen–Macaulay over it; (3) for every Serre weight σ (an irreducible representation killed by ϖ), M∞(σ) is supported on the special fibre of R∞^{ψ,σ} and maximal Cohen–Macaulay over it. It is minimal if M∞(σ°(τ)) is locally free of rank one over the generic fibre whenever that generic fibre is regular.
hypotheses: Here R∞^{ψ,τ} is the potentially crystalline Hodge type 0 (that is, weights (1,0) after BHHMS's normalisation) quotient and R∞^{ψ,σ} the crystalline quotient of Hodge type σ.
Maximal Cohen–Macaulay is in the sense of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3: depth equals the dimension of the ring over which it is taken.
proofSteps: Take EGS15 Definitions 6.1.1 and 6.1.3 verbatim in content, specialised to one place v with K = GL₂(O_{F_v}) and the BHHMS central character ψ^{−1}|I_{F_v}.

Lemma (EGS15 6.1.4): if X∞^{ψ,τ} is regular then M∞(σ°(τ)) is free over it; if its generic fibre is regular then M∞(σ°(τ))[1/p] is locally free. Proof: maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules over regular local rings are free by Auslander–Buchsbaum (R03.3/free-of-maximal-depth-regular-local).
Extend from finite length objects to finitely generated ones by M∞(σ) = lim_n M∞(σ/ϖⁿσ) (EGS15 §6.4).

nodes.title: The patching functor of Shimura curves at v
nodes.statement: Let a generic global datum be given. For each w ∈ S_p ∖ {v} fix a tame inertial type τ_w such that JH(σ(τ_w^∨)) contains exactly one Serre weight σ_w of W(r̄_w^∨), and a GL₂(O_{F_w})-stable lattice σ°(τ_w^∨), free over W(𝔽); put σ_p^v = ⊗_{w∈S_p∖{v}} σ°(τ_w^∨), a representation of ∏_{w∈S∖{v}} U_w through its quotient ∏_{w∈S_p∖{v}} GL₂(O_{F_w}). Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching of the modules M(σ_p^v ⊗ σ_v) at auxiliary levels produces integers q ≥ [F:ℚ], the rings S∞ → R∞ of GK.1/patched-deformation-ring and an exact functor M∞ = M∞^{σ_p^v} : σ_v ↦ M∞(σ_p^v ⊗ σ_v) from continuous representations of K = GL₂(O_{F_v}) on finitely generated W(𝔽)-modules with central character ψ^{−1}|I_{F_v} to finitely generated R∞-modules, such that: M∞(σ_v)/(x₁, …, x_{4|S|+q−1}) ≅ M(σ_p^v ⊗ σ_v), compatibly with a surjection R∞/(x) ↠ R_S^{loc-cond}, where R_S^{loc-cond} is the global deformation ring with the specified local conditions; the action of R^loc on M∞(σ_v) factors through the fixed-determinant quotient at v and, at w ∈ S_p ∖ {v}, through R_{r̄_w}^{(0,−1),τ_w,ψ_w}; M∞(σ_v) is free over S∞ when σ_v is free over W(𝔽), and free over S∞/(p) when σ_v is free over 𝔽; and M∞ is a fixed-determinant patching functor.
hypotheses: The weights and types at w ∈ S_p ∖ {v} come from EGS15 Proposition 3.5.1 (a type isolating one weight), part of the recorded gap on tame types owned by LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartII.

The construction uses one choice (non-principal ultrafilter or diagonal subsequence) for all σ_v simultaneously, so that M∞ is a functor: there are only countably many isomorphism classes of finite length σ_v (EGS15 §6.4).
The central character convention is BHHMS's: (𝔸_F^∞)^× acts through ψ^{−1} (BHHMS Remark 8.1.3(i)).
proofSteps: Taylor–Wiles data Q_N (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5; the generator count in Gee's convention, R04.5/taylor-wiles-generator-count, gives q − [F:ℚ] + |S| − 1 patching variables, with q ≥ [F:ℚ] for p > 5 and r̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible) at level N, with the spaces at auxiliary level free over the group rings of the Δ_{Q_N} (GK.0/non-eisenstein-freeness; R18.3/tw-freeness is its definite Taylor–Wiles instance).

Patch the modules M(σ_p^v ⊗ σ_v)_{Q_N} with their framings over S∞ by the finite-data extraction of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5 (patching-extraction, patched-module, patched-ring-action), simultaneously for all finite length σ_v; extend to finitely generated σ_v by inverse limits.

The functor σ ↦ S(σ)_𝔪 is contravariantly exact (GK.0/residual-eigenspaces); its dual multiplicity module M is covariantly exact at every auxiliary level. Patching preserves this exact system, giving covariant exactness of M∞.

Support at w ∈ S_p ∖ {v}: local–global compatibility for the type σ°(τ_w^∨) (EGS15 §6.4). Support at v for lattices in types: local–global compatibility; for Serre weights: the Gee–Kisin support statements that EGS15 §6.4 cites as Corollaries 5.6.4 and 4.5.7 of the 2012 version (the Breuil–Mézard gap).
Maximal Cohen–Macaulay: M∞(σ°(τ)) is finite free over the regular ring S∞ and dim R∞^{ψ,τ} = dim S∞, so Auslander–Buchsbaum gives the maximal depth (EGS15 §6.4).

sources.locator: §8.1, (62) and the definition of M∞^{σ_p^v}, pp. 88; Remark 8.1.3, pp. 88–89
sources.match: The representation σ_p^v built from tame types at the other places above p isolating one weight each, and the patching functor σ_v ↦ M∞(σ_p^v ⊗ σ_v) on representations of GL₂(O_{F_v}) with central character ψ^{−1}, valued in finite R∞-modules, defined as in EGS15 §§6.2 and 6.4 with the corrections of Remark 8.1.3.

Functorial Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching of the spaces M(σ) gives S∞, R∞, S∞ → R∞ and an exact functor with augmentation isomorphisms, support through the type and weight quotients, freeness over S∞ for free σ, and the fixed-determinant patching functor property.

nodes.title: Fibres of the patching functor at the maximal ideal
nodes.statement: For every continuous representation σ_v of K = GL₂(O_{F_v}) on a finitely generated W(𝔽)-module with central character ψ^{−1}|I_{F_v} on which some V_v ⊆ 1 + pM₂(O_{F_v}), normal in K, acts trivially, there are natural isomorphisms of finite-dimensional 𝔽-vector spaces M∞(σ_v)/𝔪∞ ≅ Hom_{U_v/V_v}(σ_v, Hom_{U^v/V^v}(⊗_{w∈S_p∖{v}}σ_w, Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹_ét(X_V ×_F F̄, 𝔽))))^∨ ≅ Hom_K(σ_v, π)^∨ in the indefinite case, with S(V, 𝔽)[𝔪] in place of the r̄-part in the definite case, where π is the weighted representation of GK.0/infinite-level-representation and σ_w the unique weight of W(r̄_w^∨) in JH(σ(τ_w^∨)). In particular M∞(σ_v) ≠ 0 if and only if JH(σ_v/pσ_v) ∩ W(r̄_v^∨) ≠ ∅.
hypotheses: V_w = U_w for w ∉ S_p and V_w ⊆ 1 + pM₂(O_{F_w}) normal in GL₂(O_{F_w}) for w ∈ S_p.
The fibre is taken at the maximal ideal 𝔪∞ of R∞, after the augmentation of S∞.
proofSteps: Reduce M∞(σ_v) modulo (x₁, …) and then modulo the maximal ideal of R_S^{univ}: by the augmentation isomorphism this is M(σ_p^v ⊗ σ_v)/𝔪, which in the indefinite case is dual to the r̄-part of S(σ_p^v ⊗ σ_v)[𝔪] by the evaluation isomorphism (GK.0/residual-eigenspaces).

Hochschild–Serre for the normal subgroup V ⊆ U (GK.0/non-eisenstein-freeness: finite quotient acting freely, non-Eisenstein localisation) identifies the r̄-part at level U with coefficients σ_p^v ⊗ σ_v with Hom_{U/V}((σ_p^v ⊗ σ_v)/ϖ, r̄-part at level V) (BHHMS (64), citing the proofs of BDJ10 Lemma 4.11 and Breuil–Diamond Lemme 3.6.2).

Since JH(σ°(τ_w^∨)/ϖ) contains only one weight σ_w of W(r̄_w^∨), and weights outside W(r̄_w^∨) contribute nothing by GK.0/bdj-weight-theorem, the type lattice at w may be replaced by σ_w; passing to the colimit over V_v gives Hom_K(σ_v, π)^∨ (BHHMS (68)).

Nonvanishing: use M∞(σ_v)/p ≅ M∞(σ_v/pσ_v), Nakayama for the finite R∞-module, and exactness. The finite-length representation σ_v/pσ_v has a constituent in W(r̄_v^∨) exactly when M∞(σ_v) is nonzero. Jordan–Hölder factors are not assigned directly to an infinite-length O-lattice.

nodes.title: The big patched module with its GL₂(F_v)-action
nodes.statement: With the data of GK.1/shimura-curve-patching-functor (and the same σ_p^v, with Hecke operators at the places of S′ forgotten), the patching construction of Dotto–Le §6.2 (a variant of Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin §2 and Scholze §9) produces a profinite R∞⟦K⟧-module M∞, K = GL₂(O_{F_v}), with an R∞-linear continuous action of GL₂(F_v) extending the K-action, such that: M∞ is finite free over S∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧; M∞ is finite projective over S∞⟦K⟧_Z, the largest quotient of S∞⟦K⟧ on which the centre of K acts through ψ|I_{F_v}; M∞/𝔪∞M∞ ≅ π^∨ for the weighted π of GK.0; and for every continuous σ_v as in GK.1 with central character ψ^{−1}|I_{F_v}, M∞(σ_v) ≅ Hom^{cont}_{W(𝔽)⟦K⟧}(M∞, σ_v^∨)^∨, where (−)^∨ = Hom^{cont}_{W(𝔽)}(−, E/W(𝔽)). If moreover p is inert in F, then M∞ ⊗_{S∞} W(𝔽) ≅ Hom_{W(𝔽)}(Ĥ¹(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}}, W(𝔽)) (resp. the dual of Ŝ(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}} in the definite case), compatibly with surjections R∞ ⊗_{S∞} W(𝔽) ↠ R_{r̄,S∪{w₁}}^ψ ↠ T̂(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}}.
hypotheses: Here K₁ = 1 + pM₂(O_{F_v}) and Z₁ the centre of K₁; K₁/Z₁ is a uniform pro-p group of dimension 3f (p > 2, F_v unramified).

The construction uses the same Taylor–Wiles data and patching choice as GK.1/shimura-curve-patching-functor, so that the two are compatible; a choice of basis of the universal deformation over R_{r̄,S∪{w₁}}^ψ is among the choices (BHHMS §8.5).
proofSteps: Replace K^v by U^v and the representation V of Dotto–Le §6.1 by σ_p^v, and forget the Hecke operators T_w at w ∈ S′ (no multiplicity one is needed); patch the dual completed cohomology at Taylor–Wiles levels as in Dotto–Le §6.2 (BHHMS proof of Theorem 8.4.1 (ii)).

Freeness over S∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧ and projectivity over S∞⟦K⟧_Z: at each auxiliary level and each finite quotient K₁/V of K₁ the dual 𝔪-localised cohomology is free over the finite group ring (GK.0/non-eisenstein-freeness, with R03.5/projectivity-by-derived-coinvariants for the finite groups); patch these finite S∞/J-modules (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5) compatibly in J and V and pass to the inverse limit, which gives freeness over S∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧. The same construction for definite unitary groups and definite quaternion algebras with p split is CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.5 (an analogue, not a supplier here).
The fibre M∞/𝔪∞ ≅ π^∨ and the comparison with the patching functor M∞(σ_v) = Hom(M∞, σ_v^∨)^∨ follow from the construction and from (68) (GK.1/patched-fibre-identity).

When p is inert, reducing modulo (x₁, …) recovers the dual of the localized completed cohomology and the surjections onto the global deformation ring and the big Hecke algebra (BHHMS (84), citing CEGGPS §2, Scholze §9, Dotto–Le §6).

nodes.title: Grade, dimension and Cohen–Macaulay modules over Iwasawa algebras
nodes.statement: Let K be a compact p-adic analytic group and Λ = O⟦K⟧. For a finitely generated Λ-module M the grade is j_Λ(M) = inf{i : Ext^i_Λ(M, Λ) ≠ 0} (∞ if all vanish); when K is pro-p, Λ is local with residue field k and depth_Λ(M) = inf{i : Ext^i_Λ(k, M) ≠ 0}; when Λ is Auslander regular, the dimension is δ_Λ(M) = gld(Λ) − j_Λ(M). A nonzero finitely generated Λ-module M is Cohen–Macaulay if Ext^i_Λ(M, Λ) ≠ 0 for exactly one i. For K torsion-free pro-p, Λ is Auslander regular with gld(Λ) = depth_Λ(Λ) = 1 + dim K, the Auslander–Buchsbaum equality pd_Λ(M) + depth_Λ(M) = 1 + dim K holds, pd_Λ(M) = max{i : Ext^i_Λ(M, Λ) ≠ 0}, and M is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if depth_Λ(M) = δ_Λ(M). For K uniform, the same applies to A = Λ ⊗̂_O O⟦x₁, …, x_r⟧ = O⟦K × ℤ_p^r⟧, with gld(A) = 1 + dim K + r.
hypotheses: Left and right modules are interchanged by g ↦ g^{−1}, so the definitions do not depend on the side.

For an arbitrary compact p-adic analytic K the ring Λ is only semilocal and need not be Auslander regular; grades are then computed on a normal open torsion-free pro-p subgroup (Lemma A.7 of Gee–Newton).
proofSteps: Take grade, dimension and Auslander regularity of Iwasawa algebras of torsion-free uniform groups from CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.5 (Venjakob's theorem), and depth from the local ring structure of Λ for pro-p K; the Auslander–Buchsbaum equality and the formula for projective dimension over Λ are Venjakob's Theorem 6.2 and Corollary 6.3 (Gee–Newton Proposition A.4), stated here because CC.5 does not.

Define the Cohen–Macaulay predicate by the single nonvanishing Ext degree (Gee–Newton Definition A.5); prove its equivalence with depth = δ from the Auslander–Buchsbaum equality and the formula for projective dimension (Gee–Newton Proposition A.4 and Remark A.6, citing Venjakob Theorem 6.2 and Corollary 6.3).
For A = O⟦K × ℤ_p^r⟧ apply the same statements to the uniform group K × ℤ_p^r.

nodes.title: Freeness over the support from a submodule and a quotient
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, N ⊆ M A-modules and r ≥ 1 such that (i) N and M/N are free of rank r over their scheme-theoretic supports A/Ann_A(N) and A/Ann_A(M/N); (ii) M is generated by r elements; (iii) Ann_A(M/N)/Ann_A(M) ≅ A/Ann_A(N) as A-modules. Then M is free of rank r over A/Ann_A(M).
hypotheses: No Noetherian or local hypothesis is needed; finiteness enters only through the generation by r elements.
proofSteps: Replace A by A/Ann_A(M); put I = Ann_A(M/N) and choose a surjection f : A^r ↠ M.

The composite A^r → M → M/N factors through (A/I)^r; as M/N ≅ (A/I)^r, the induced surjection (A/I)^r ↠ M/N is an isomorphism (a surjective endomorphism of a finitely generated module is bijective: Stacks 05G8, Matsumura Theorem 2.4).
The snake lemma makes I^r → N surjective; since I ≅ A/Ann_A(N) and N ≅ (A/Ann_A(N))^r, the same fact makes I^r → N bijective, so f is an isomorphism.

sources.match: If N ⊆ M with N and M/N free of rank r over their supports, M generated by r elements and Ann(M/N)/Ann(M) ≅ A/Ann(N), then M is free of rank r over its support.
A surjective module endomorphism of a finite module over a commutative ring is an isomorphism.

acceptance: Hypothesis (iii) is an isomorphism of A-modules, not merely of abelian groups.
The conclusion is freeness over A/Ann_A(M), with the same rank r.

nodes.title: Freeness of fibre products over their supports
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative Noetherian local ring, M₁, M₂, M nonzero R-modules each free of rank r over its scheme-theoretic support, and M_i ↠ M surjections. Then Ann_R(M₁ ×_M M₂) = Ann_R(M₁) ∩ Ann_R(M₂), and the following are equivalent: (i) M₁ ×_M M₂ is free of rank r over its scheme-theoretic support; (ii) Ann_R(M) = Ann_R(M₁) + Ann_R(M₂); (iii) Ann_R(M) ⊆ Ann_R(M₁) + Ann_R(M₂).
hypotheses: R local is used through Nakayama to reduce to rank one; the annihilator identity holds for any ring because the maps M_i → M are surjective.
proofSteps: Write M_i = (R/I_i)^r and M = (R/I)^r with I_i ⊆ I; after changing bases the surjections are the natural maps, so M₁ ×_M M₂ ≅ (R/I₁ ×_{R/I} R/I₂)^r and by Nakayama one reduces to r = 1.

For r = 1 the diagonal R → R/I₁ ×_{R/I} R/I₂ has kernel I₁ ∩ I₂; it is surjective iff every pair (a, b) with a ≡ b mod I is congruent to some c modulo I₁ and I₂, iff I ⊆ I₁ + I₂ (Chinese remainder argument). Surjectivity is exactly cyclicity, i.e. freeness of rank one over R/(I₁ ∩ I₂).
(ii) ⇔ (iii) because I₁ + I₂ ⊆ I always holds. BHHMS cite Hu–Wang Lemma 8.11 for the rank-one case.

sources.match: For nonzero modules free of rank r over their supports with surjections onto a common module, the fibre product has annihilator the intersection, and it is free of rank r over its support iff the annihilator of the target is the sum of the two annihilators, iff it is contained in that sum; the proof reduces to rank one.

acceptance: All three modules are nonzero and free of the same rank r over their supports.
The equivalence uses the given surjections, not arbitrary maps to M.

nodes.title: Grade and dimension under power-series variables (Gee–Newton)
nodes.statement: Let K be uniform pro-p, Λ = O⟦K⟧, Ω = Λ/ϖΛ = k⟦K⟧, A = Λ ⊗̂_O O⟦x₁, …, x_r⟧ and B = Λ ⊗̂_O O⟦y₁, …, y_s⟧ with the map A → B induced by a local O-algebra map O⟦x⟧ → O⟦y⟧. For a finitely generated A-module M and x ∈ {ϖ, x₁, …, x_r}: (1) if xM = 0 then δ_A(M) = δ_{A/x}(M); if M is x-torsion free then δ_A(M) = 1 + δ_{A/x}(M/xM), equivalently j_A(M) = j_{A/x}(M/xM); (2) in general j_A(M) ≥ j_{A/x}(M/xM), hence j_A(M) ≥ j_Λ(M/(x₁, …, x_r)M) ≥ j_Ω(M/(ϖ, x₁, …, x_r)M); (3) for a finitely generated B-module M which is finitely generated over A, δ_A(M) = δ_B(M); (4) for a finitely generated Ω-module M, δ_Ω(M) = limsup_n log_n dim_k(M/J_Ω^n M), J_Ω the Jacobson radical.
hypotheses: K uniform pro-p, so that A and B are Iwasawa algebras of the uniform groups K × ℤ_p^r and K × ℤ_p^s and hence Auslander regular.
Statement (4) is the Gelfand–Kirillov description of the canonical dimension (Ardakov–Brown); it links grades to the growth of invariants used in MP.4.
proofSteps: (1) Base change spectral sequence for Ext along A → A/x, with Ext^j_A(A/x, A) = A/x concentrated in j = 1; for x-torsion free M, Levasseur's inequality j_A(M/xM) ≥ 1 + j_A(M) and Nakayama on the lowest Ext (Gee–Newton Lemma A.15).
(2) Filter M by x-power torsion; use the minimum formula for grades in short exact sequences and (1) on the graded pieces (Lemma A.16).

(3) J_A B = BJ_A and J_AJ_B = J_BJ_A because the x_i become central (Lemma A.17); M/J_AM is finite length over B, so the J_A- and J_B-adic filtrations are cofinal and the Gelfand–Kirillov dimensions (4) agree for ϖ-torsion and ϖ-torsion-free modules, hence in general by dévissage (Lemmas A.18–A.19).
(4) Ardakov–Brown Proposition 5.4(3), as quoted in Gee–Newton Proposition A.13 (J_Ω-adic growth; MP.4/gk-dimension records the equivalent growth of invariants under the p-power filtration).

sources.match: Grades drop by at most the expected amount on passing to x-quotients and are preserved for x-torsion-free modules; the canonical dimension of a module finite over both A and B is the same over A and over B; over Ω it is the Gelfand–Kirillov dimension.

acceptance: The inequality j_A(M) ≥ j_Ω(M/(ϖ, x)M) is stated in this direction; equality needs flatness (GK.2/iwasawa-miracle-flatness).
(3) requires M finitely generated over A, not merely over B.

nodes.title: Cohen–Macaulay transfer along A → B (Gee–Newton)
nodes.statement: In the setting of GK.2/iwasawa-grade-and-power-series, for every B-module M, depth_A(M) ≤ depth_B(M); and if M is a finitely generated B-module which is finitely generated and Cohen–Macaulay as an A-module, then M is a Cohen–Macaulay B-module with depth_B(M) = δ_B(M) = δ_A(M).
hypotheses: The depth comparison is an inequality; the reverse inequality also holds but is not needed.
proofSteps: Injective B-modules are injective over Λ because B is flat over Λ (Lemma A.21); compute Ext_Λ(k, M) as a complex of S = k⟦y⟧-modules and compare depths over R = k⟦x⟧ and S through the forgetful functor (Lemmas A.22–A.25).

For complexes of modules over commutative Noetherian local rings, depth along a local map can only drop under restriction of scalars (Iyengar's depth for complexes; Lemma A.27), giving depth_A(M) ≤ depth_B(M) (Lemma A.28).

If M is CM over A: δ_A(M) = depth_A(M) ≤ depth_B(M) ≤ δ_B(M) (Auslander–Buchsbaum over the Iwasawa algebra B, GK.2/iwasawa-cohen-macaulay) and δ_A(M) = δ_B(M) by GK.2/iwasawa-grade-and-power-series (3), so all are equal (Corollary A.29).

sources.locator: §A.20: Lemmas A.21–A.28 and Corollary A.29, pp. 47–49
sources.match: Depth over A is at most depth over B, and a module finite over both that is Cohen–Macaulay over A is Cohen–Macaulay over B with the same dimension.

acceptance: The hypothesis is that M is finitely generated over A as well as over B.
The conclusion identifies depth_B(M), δ_B(M) and δ_A(M).

nodes.title: Miracle flatness over Iwasawa algebras (Gee–Newton)
nodes.statement: Let K be uniform pro-p, A = O⟦K⟧ ⊗̂_O O⟦x₁, …, x_r⟧, Ω = k⟦K⟧, and M a finitely generated Cohen–Macaulay A-module. Then M is flat over O⟦x₁, …, x_r⟧ if and only if j_A(M) = j_Ω(M/(ϖ, x₁, …, x_r)M).
hypotheses: M is Cohen–Macaulay over A in the sense of GK.2/iwasawa-cohen-macaulay; in particular M ≠ 0.
proofSteps: If M is flat, (ϖ, x₁, …, x_r) is an M-regular sequence (M/(ϖ, x)M ≠ 0 by Nakayama), and GK.2/iwasawa-grade-and-power-series (1) gives the equality of grades.

Conversely, for x ∈ {ϖ, x_i} show by induction: j_A(M) = j_{A/x}(M/xM) (from the chain of inequalities in (2) and the hypothesis); x is M-regular (a nonzero x-power torsion submodule would have the full dimension by purity of Cohen–Macaulay modules, Venjakob Propositions 3.5 and 3.9, contradicting the grade equality); and M/xM is Cohen–Macaulay over A/x (long exact Ext sequence).

The regular sequence gives flatness modulo every power of the maximal ideal 𝔞 = (ϖ, x₁, …, x_r) of B = O⟦x₁, …, x_r⟧. For every ideal I of B, I ⊗_B M is finitely generated over the Noetherian algebra A; since 𝔞A lies in its Jacobson radical it is 𝔞-adically separated. Apply the adic flatness criterion to these tensor modules, not just to M (Gee–Newton proof of Proposition A.30, p. 50, adapting Stacks 00MK / Matsumura Theorem 22.3). This proves B-flatness although M need not be finite over B.

sources.locator: Proposition A.30 and proof, pp. 49–50 (BHHMS cite it as Corollary A.30)
sources.match: A finitely generated Cohen–Macaulay module over the Iwasawa algebra with power-series coefficients is flat over the coefficient power-series ring exactly when its grade equals the grade of its reduction modulo (ϖ, x) over k⟦K⟧.
The local criterion of flatness for ideal-separated modules.

acceptance: The grade on the right is over Ω = k⟦K⟧ of the full reduction modulo (ϖ, x₁, …, x_r).
This is the noncommutative analogue of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3/miracle-flatness-finite-modules, which it does not replace.

nodes.title: Patched modules of finite length representations are maximal Cohen–Macaulay
nodes.statement: For every smooth representation σ of K = GL₂(O_{F_v}) on a finite length W(𝔽)-module with central character ψ^{−1}|I_{F_v}, the R∞-module M∞(σ) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over its scheme-theoretic support R∞/Ann_{R∞}(M∞(σ)); in particular this support has no embedded associated prime.
hypotheses: M∞ = M∞^{σ_p^v} is the patching functor of GK.1/shimura-curve-patching-functor; finite length means killed by a power of p and of finite length as a W(𝔽)-module.
proofSteps: If M∞(σ) = 0 there is nothing to prove. For each Serre weight σ_v with M∞(σ_v) ≠ 0, the patching-functor property (3) makes M∞(σ_v) Cohen–Macaulay of Krull dimension d independent of σ_v (all weight loci have dimension dim S∞ − 1).
By exactness, dim M∞(σ) is the maximum of dim M∞(σ_v) over the constituents σ_v of σ, so it equals d, and every nonzero M∞(σ_v) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R∞/Ann_{R∞}(M∞(σ)).

Being maximal Cohen–Macaulay over a fixed Noetherian local ring with residue field 𝔽 is stable under extensions (characterise depth by vanishing of Ext^i(𝔽, −) in low degrees), so M∞(σ) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay.

sources.match: For any smooth K-representation on a finite length W(𝔽)-module, the patched module is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over its scheme-theoretic support, by the dimension independence of weight loci, exactness and stability of maximal Cohen–Macaulayness under extensions.

acceptance: The ring over which maximal Cohen–Macaulayness is asserted is the scheme-theoretic support R∞/Ann_{R∞}(M∞(σ)).
The argument uses the depth characterisation by Ext from the residue field, which is extension-stable.

nodes.title: Freeness for Serre weights and for lattices in tame types
nodes.statement: There is an integer r ≥ 1 such that: (i) for every σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨), M∞(σ_v) is free of rank r over its scheme-theoretic support, which is formally smooth over 𝔽; (ii) for every tame inertial type τ with JH(σ(τ)) ∩ W(r̄_v^∨) ≠ ∅ and every K-stable W(𝔽)-lattice σ°(τ) in σ(τ) with irreducible cosocle, M∞(σ°(τ)) is free of rank r over its scheme-theoretic support, which is the domain R∞^{(1,0),τ}.
hypotheses: Generic global datum; M∞ = M∞^{σ_p^v}. MP.5/finite-weight-hulls covers the principal-series intervals; the cuspidal types (second inertial shape at v) and EGS15 §§5.1, 10.1 are part of the tame-type gap.

The structure of the tame potentially Barsotti–Tate rings (formal smoothness, domain property, special fibres; EGS15 Theorem 7.2.1) and the description of the constituents of lattices in tame types (EGS15 §5.1, Propositions 3.5.1–3.5.2) come from the gaps owned by LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartII.
proofSteps: By EGS15 §5.1 the lattice is σ_J°(τ) for a unique subset J in a set P_τ; its constituents in W(r̄_v^∨) are indexed by a subset W ⊆ P_τ, and for capped intervals 𝒥 ⊆ W there are subquotients σ^𝒥 with exactly those constituents (EGS15 Definition 10.1.4).

Supports: R∞/Ann(M∞(σ^𝒥)) is reduced, being generically reduced by dévissage (the supports of the M∞(σ_v) are reduced, irreducible, pairwise distinct and of equal dimension, and σ^𝒥 is multiplicity free) and without embedded primes by GK.3/patched-maximal-cohen-macaulay; hence it equals the ideal I_𝒥 of EGS15 §10.1.

|𝒥| ≤ 2: there is a tame type τ′ and a lattice with M∞(σ°(τ′)) ≅ M∞(σ^𝒥), and R∞^{(1,0),τ′} is regular, so M∞(σ^𝒥) is free (EGS15 Lemma 6.1.4); for |𝒥| = 2 freeness over a power series ring over 𝔽⟦X₁, X₂⟧/(X₁X₂) forces equal ranks of the two weights, and connectedness of W(r̄_v^∨) by nonsplit extensions (EGS15 Proposition 3.5.2) gives one rank r for all weights.

|𝒥| > 2 with a unique minimal element 𝒥₀: M∞(σ^𝒥) is generated by r elements (as in EGS15 Theorem 10.1.1, using Le's Lemma 4.5 in place of EGS15 Lemma 10.1.13), and GK.2/freeness-from-extension with N = M∞(σ^{{𝒥₀}}) gives freeness; with two minimal elements, write M∞(σ^𝒥) as a fibre product over smaller capped intervals and use GK.2/fibre-product-freeness.

(ii): for 𝒥 = W this gives M∞(σ_J°(τ))/p free of rank r over R̄∞^{(1,0),τ}; lift a basis by Nakayama to a surjection (R∞^{(1,0),τ})^r ↠ M∞(σ°(τ)) which is an isomorphism mod p; its kernel satisfies p·ker = ker because M∞(σ°(τ)) is p-torsion free, so the kernel vanishes.

sources.match: A single rank r ≥ 1 such that patched modules of modular Serre weights are free of rank r over formally smooth supports, and patched modules of lattices with irreducible cosocle in tame types meeting the modular weights are free of rank r over domain supports; proved along EGS15 Theorem 10.1.1 by induction over capped intervals.
The case r = 1 (multiplicity one) by the same induction; freeness over regular type loci; the existence of types isolating one or containing all modular weights.

For M″ ⊆ M′ ⊆ M over a local ring with M′/M″ and M′ minimally generated by the same number of elements, M″ ⊆ 𝔪M, and M/M″ and M are minimally generated by the same number of elements if M is finitely generated.

acceptance: One rank r serves all modular weights and all lattices in (ii).
The supports in (ii) are the type quotients R∞^{(1,0),τ}, domains by the gap owner's theorem.

nodes.title: Lattices in sums of locally algebraic types
nodes.statement: Let σ = ⊕_{i=1}^m σ_i^{n_i} with m, n_i ≥ 1, where the σ_i = σ_i^{sm} ⊗_E σ_i^{alg} are pairwise nonisomorphic absolutely irreducible locally algebraic representations of K over E, each σ_i^{sm} ⊗ Q̄_p in the image of the inertial local Langlands correspondence τ ↦ σ(τ), and with ∪_i JH(σ_i) ∩ W(r̄_v^∨) ≠ ∅; let σ° be any K-stable W(𝔽)-lattice in σ. Then (i) M∞(σ°) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over its scheme-theoretic support S = R∞/Ann_{R∞}(M∞(σ°)), which is reduced; (ii) M∞(σ°) ⊗_{W(𝔽)} E is locally free over S[1/p], which is formally smooth over E. Every irreducible tame smooth σ_i^{sm} that is not a twist of the Steinberg representation of GL₂(k) satisfies the image hypothesis.
hypotheses: The uses in this roadmap have tame smooth parts and algebraic parts V(α_j) or trivial; the image hypothesis is then supplied by the tame-type gap (BHHMS Remark 8.2.5, citing Breuil–Mézard Theorem 2.1.1.4 and Emerton–Gee–Herzig Proposition 2.4.1).
proofSteps: By exactness, M∞(σ°)[1/p] ≅ ⊕_i M∞(σ_i°)[1/p]^{n_i} for lattices σ_i° (BHHMS (71)).

By Taylor–Wiles–Kisin, R∞ acts on M∞(σ_i°) through a reduced equidimensional p-torsion-free quotient R∞/I_i whose support is a union of irreducible components (CEGGPS Lemmas 4.17–4.18, proved there for unitary groups and by the same argument here; the notion is DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6/supported-on-components). The Spec (R∞/I_i)[1/p] are disjoint because the σ_i are pairwise distinct, so S[1/p] ≅ ∏_i (R∞/I_i)[1/p] by the Chinese remainder theorem (BHHMS (72)).

Each (R∞/I_i)[1/p] is a union of components of a potentially crystalline generic fibre, which is formally smooth over E (Kisin; LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3/pcris-generic-smooth), hence regular; S has no p-torsion, so S is reduced.

M∞(σ°)/p ≅ M∞(σ°/p) is Cohen–Macaulay by GK.3/patched-maximal-cohen-macaulay and p is a nonzerodivisor, so M∞(σ°) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over S; M∞(σ°)[1/p] is Cohen–Macaulay over the regular ring S[1/p], hence locally free by Auslander–Buchsbaum.

sources.locator: Corollary 8.2.4 and proof, (71)–(72), pp. 92–93; Remark 8.2.5, p. 93
sources.match: Patched modules of lattices in sums of pairwise distinct locally algebraic types meeting the modular weights are maximal Cohen–Macaulay over reduced supports and locally free after inverting p over formally smooth generic fibres; tame non-Steinberg smooth types are in the image of the inertial local Langlands correspondence.

Patched modules of lattices in types are supported on reduced p-torsion-free quotients whose support is a union of irreducible components, and are locally free of rank one on the regular locus of the generic fibre.

acceptance: The supports of the summands are disjoint after inverting p because the σ_i are pairwise nonisomorphic.
Local freeness is asserted after inverting p only.

nodes.title: Freeness for the projective lift of a modular Serre weight
nodes.statement: Let σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨), P_{σ_v} = Proj_{GL₂(k)}σ_v and P̃_{σ_v} its finite free projective lift to W(𝔽)[GL₂(k)], inflated to K. Then π^{K₁} ≅ D₀(r̄_v^∨)^{⊕r} as GL₂(k)-representations, dim_𝔽 Hom_K(P_{σ_v}, π) = r, and M∞(P̃_{σ_v}) is free of rank r over R∞/∩_τ p_τ, where τ runs over the tame inertial types with σ_v ∈ JH(σ(τ)) and p_τ = ker(R∞ ↠ R∞^{(1,0),τ}).
hypotheses: r is the rank of GK.3/weight-and-type-freeness; D₀(r̄_v^∨) is the Breuil–Paškūnas representation of ModpRepresentationsOfGL2OverLocalFields MP.3/diamond-socle.

The upper embedding W = π^{K₁} ↪ D₀(r̄_v^∨)^{⊕r} follows from BHHMS Proposition 8.2.6 and LMS22 Proposition 4.6. Being an isomorphism on socles alone does not prove it is an isomorphism. The reverse embedding is the independent global extension argument below.
P̃_{σ_v}[1/p] ≅ ⊕_τ σ(τ), each tame type with σ_v ∈ JH(σ(τ)) occurring once (tame-type gap).
proofSteps: Generation by r elements: by Nakayama and GK.1/patched-fibre-identity it suffices that dim Hom_K(P_{σ_v}, π) = dim Hom_{GL₂(k)}(P_{σ_v}, W) = r for W = π^{K₁}. By GK.3/weight-and-type-freeness (i), dim Hom(σ, W) = r for each modular weight; since Hom(P_{σ_v}, D₀/soc D₀) = 0 it suffices to embed W into D₀(r̄_v^∨)^{⊕r}, equivalently to find a surjection (D₀^∨)^{⊕r} ↠ W^∨, which follows as in Le–Morra–Schraen Lemma 4.5 and Proposition 4.6 with 1 replaced by r.

For the reverse embedding, embed R′ = soc(D₀^{⊕r}) into the weighted π using the weight theorem and its multiplicity r. Put R = D₀^{⊕r}; by the defining property of D₀, R/R′ has no modular Serre weight, so Hom_K(R/R′, π) = 0. Apply the argument of Breuil Lemma 9.2 to the finite-level spaces: localisation makes Hom(−, S)_𝔪 exact by GK.0/non-eisenstein-freeness; the zero quotient Hom space remains zero after localisation by Nakayama. Restriction Hom(R, S)_𝔪 → Hom(R′, S)_𝔪 is therefore an isomorphism. Taking the residual Hecke eigenspace, the Galois multiplicity space, and the fixed weights away from v preserves this isomorphism. The socle embedding extends uniquely to R → π and is injective since every nonzero submodule of R meets its socle. Thus D₀^{⊕r} ↪ W. Both modules are finite-dimensional, so together with the upper embedding this gives W ≅ D₀^{⊕r}, without GK.4 or GK.5.

nodes.title: The glued lattices L_j and the comparison lattices N_j
nodes.statement: Fix σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨); write P = P_{σ_v} and P̃ = P̃_{σ_v} for its projective envelope over GL₂(k) and the projective W(𝔽)[GL₂(k)]-lift, inflated to K = GL₂(O_{F_v}). For j ∈ {0, …, f − 1} let V(α_j) = (Sym²(W(𝔽)²) ⊗ det^{−1})^{(j)}, the algebraic representation of K through the embedding σ_j, put R_{2,j} = V(α_j) ⊗_{W(𝔽)} P̃ and, with the fixed embedding ι_j : P ↪ R_{2,j}/pR_{2,j} of MP.8/projective-lattice, R′_{2,j} = {x ∈ R_{2,j} : x mod p ∈ ι_j(P)}: a K-stable lattice with pR_{2,j} ⊆ R′_{2,j} ⊆ R_{2,j}, R′_{2,j}/pR_{2,j} ≅ P, (R′_{2,j}/pR′_{2,j})_{K₁} ≅ P and a K-equivariant exact sequence 0 → P_{σ_{1,j}} ⊕ P_{σ_{2,j}} → R′_{2,j}/pR′_{2,j} → P → 0, where σ_{1,j}, σ_{2,j} are the weights F(λ ∓ α_j) for σ_v = F(λ). Put L_{−1} = P̃ and L_j = L_{j−1} ×_P R′_{2,j} (the fibre product over the reductions modulo p), a K-stable lattice in P̃[1/p] ⊕ ⊕_{j′≤j} R_{2,j′}[1/p]; then L_{f−1} is the lattice R of MP.8/projective-lattice. For a tame type τ with σ_v ∈ JH(σ(τ)), let σ(τ)° be the image of P̃ in σ(τ) (the lattice with cosocle σ_v), T_{2,j} = V(α_j) ⊗ σ(τ)°, T′_{2,j} the image of R′_{2,j} → R_{2,j} ↠ T_{2,j}, Y_j = T′_{2,j}/pT_{2,j} (a quotient of P, hence of L_{j−1}) and N_j = L_{j−1} ×_{Y_j} T′_{2,j}. With τ = τ₀, the unique tame type with JH(σ(τ₀)) = W(r̄_v^∨) (r̄_v semisimple), the surjection R′_{2,j} ↠ T′_{2,j} induces a surjection L_j ↠ N_j and an exact sequence 0 → T_{2,j} →(×p) N_j → L_{j−1} → 0.

The existence and uniqueness of τ₀ is EGS15 Proposition 3.5.2 for semisimple r̄_v, part of the tame-type gap.

T′_{2,j}, Y_j, N_j: as in the proof of BHHMS Proposition 8.3.3 and before Lemma 8.3.5; the kernel of T′_{2,j} ↠ Y_j is pT_{2,j}, which gives the exact sequence for N_j (proof of BHHMS Lemma 8.3.6).

nodes.title: K₁-invariance and Loewy length of small quotients
nodes.statement: Let Q be a quotient of (Proj_{K/Z₁}σ_v)/𝔪²_{K₁}(Proj_{K/Z₁}σ_v) such that (a) the constituents of soc_K(Q) occur among those of Proj_{K/K₁}σ_v = P (up to multiplicity) and (b) [Q/soc_K(Q) : σ_v] = 1. Then rad_K(Q) and Q/S are fixed by K₁, where S is the largest σ_v-isotypic submodule of soc_K(Q). If moreover (c) the constituents of soc_K(Q) lie in W(r̄_v^∨) and (d) rad_K(Q)/soc_K(Q) has no constituent in W(r̄_v^∨), then Q has Loewy length at most 3.
hypotheses: σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨) is 2-deep, so the first-order hull statements of MP.5 apply.
proofSteps: Embed Q into ⊕_i Q_{σ_i}, one quotient with simple socle σ_i for each summand of soc_K(Q); taking radicals preserves surjections (Alperin), so rad_K(Q) ⊆ ⊕ rad_K(Q_{σ_i}) and rad_K(Q)/soc_K(Q) ↠ rad_K(Q_{σ_i})/soc_K(Q_{σ_i}); reduce to simple socle.

If soc_K(Q) ≇ σ_v then [Q : σ_v] = 1 and Q is the finite interval I(soc_K(Q), σ_v), fixed by K₁ by (a) (MP.5/first-order-weight-hulls, the uniqueness and K₁-triviality statement; Hu–Wang Theorem 2.30).

If soc_K(Q) ≅ σ_v then Q/σ_v is multiplicity free with one copy of σ_v, rad_K(Q)/σ_v is semisimple and embeds in the sum of weights with nonzero Ext¹_{K/K₁} to σ_v, so rad_K(Q) ⊆ Q^{K₁} and Q has Loewy length 3 (MP.5/first-order-weight-hulls; Hu–Wang Corollaries 2.26 and 2.31).
Q/S is K₁-fixed: any weight in its socle is in soc_K(Q) or has nonzero Ext¹_{K/Z₁} to σ_v, hence lies in JH(P), and [Q/S : σ_v] = 1.
Under (c)–(d) and soc_K(Q) ≇ σ_v: all constituents of I(soc_K(Q), σ_v) lie in W(r̄_v^∨) (MP.5/finite-weight-hulls with MP.3/tame-weight-set), so rad/soc = 0 and the Loewy length is 2.

nodes.title: M∞(R′_{2,j}) is minimally generated by r elements
nodes.statement: For every j ∈ {0, …, f − 1}, the R∞-module M∞(R′_{2,j}) is minimally generated by r elements, r the rank of GK.3/weight-and-type-freeness.
hypotheses: σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨); R′_{2,j} as in GK.4/glued-lattices.
proofSteps: Show by induction on the length of Q that M∞(Q) is minimally generated by r elements for every nonzero quotient Q of R′_{2,j}/pR′_{2,j}. Length one: Q = σ_v and GK.3/weight-and-type-freeness (i).
If soc_K(Q) contains a nonmodular weight σ then M∞(Q) = M∞(Q/σ) (GK.1/patched-fibre-identity); so assume all socle constituents are modular.

If [rad_K(Q)/soc_K(Q) : σ_v] ≠ 0, pick Q′ ⊊ Q with cosocle σ_v not in the socle; since R′_{2,j}/p is a quotient of R/pR ≅ (Proj_{K/Z₁}σ_v)/𝔪²_{K₁} (MP.8/projective-truncation, which applies because σ_v is 8-deep, hence 3-deep), relative projectivity (MP.9/relative-projectivity) makes Q′ a quotient of Q of smaller length; apply Le's Lemma 4.5 to M∞(Q′) ⊆ M∞(Q) with a socle weight σ′ of Q′.

Otherwise [Q/soc_K(Q) : σ_v] = 1, and by GK.4/loewy-length-three the quotient Q/S is K₁-fixed, hence a quotient of P; by the exact sequence of GK.4/glued-lattices the image of P_{σ_{1,j}} ⊕ P_{σ_{2,j}} in Q lies in S and is zero, so Q is a quotient of P and M∞(Q) is generated by r elements (GK.3/projective-lift-freeness); minimality from the quotient M∞(σ_v).
Conclude for R′_{2,j} by Nakayama.

nodes.title: Patched lattices in V(α_j) ⊗ τ° with cosocle σ_v
nodes.statement: Let σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨), let τ° be a representation of GL₂(k) on a finite free W(𝔽)-module with τ°[1/p] absolutely irreducible and cosoc_K(τ°) ≅ σ_v, and fix j. A K-stable lattice L in (V(α_j) ⊗ τ°)[1/p] with cosoc_K L ≅ σ_v exists and is unique up to homothety, and M∞(L) is free of rank r over its scheme-theoretic support, which is the domain R∞^{(2,−1)_j,τ}, (2,−1)_j meaning (2, −1) at σ_j and (1, 0) at the other embeddings, τ the tame type with σ(τ) ≅ τ°[1/p] ⊗ Q̄_p. For the lattices of GK.4/glued-lattices, the surjection T′_{2,j}/pT′_{2,j} ↠ Y_j induces an isomorphism M∞(T′_{2,j}/pT′_{2,j}) ≅ M∞(Y_j).
hypotheses: σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨), fixed throughout BHHMS §8.3; then σ_v = F(λ) with λ 8-deep by genericity (BHHMS Proposition 2.4.2, MP.3); τ°[1/p] is in the image of the tame inertial local Langlands correspondence (it is a tame non-Steinberg type).
The domain property of R∞^{(2,−1)_j,τ} and the reducedness of its special fibre are BHHMS Proposition 4.2.1 and Corollary 4.2.6, from the gap owned by LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartII.
proofSteps: The constituents of τ° are those of a Diamond box D_{μ,ε} (BHHMS Proposition 2.4.3 and Lemma 2.4.4, tame-type gap), so F(α_j) ⊗ τ̄° is multiplicity free (MP.6/adjoint-tensor); hence the lattice with cosocle σ_v is unique up to homothety (EGS15 Lemma 4.1.1), and it is the image L₀ of R′_{2,j} → V(α_j) ⊗ τ°.

Write 0 → W₁ → L/pL → W₂ → 0 with W₁ = (V(α_j) ⊗ τ°)/L and W₂ = L/p(V(α_j) ⊗ τ°). The constituents of W₁ are not modular (MP.6/adjoint-tensor and MP.3), so M∞(W₁) = 0; W₂ surjects onto a lattice τ′° in a tame type with cosocle σ_v, and the remaining constituents are not modular, so M∞(W₂) = M∞(τ′°) and M∞(L/pL) is generated by r elements (GK.3/weight-and-type-freeness).

The support S of M∞(L) is R∞^{(2,−1)_j,τ} because that ring is a domain; S/pS is reduced, hence it is the scheme-theoretic support of M∞(L/pL), and the Nakayama argument of GK.3/weight-and-type-freeness gives freeness of rank r.
Lemma 8.3.5: T′_{2,j}/pT′_{2,j} and Y_j are L/pL and W₂ for τ° = σ(τ)°, and M∞(L/pL) = M∞(W₂) because M∞(W₁) = 0.

nodes.title: Freeness of M∞(R′_{2,j})
nodes.statement: For j ∈ {0, …, f − 1}, M∞(R′_{2,j}) is free of rank r over R∞/∩_τ p_τ, where τ runs over the tame inertial types with σ_v ∈ JH(σ(τ)) and p_τ = ker(R∞ ↠ R∞^{(2,−1)_j,τ}).

proofSteps: By GK.4/adjoint-lattice-generation there is a surjection f : S^r ↠ M∞(R′_{2,j}), S the scheme-theoretic support.
R′_{2,j}[1/p] = R_{2,j}[1/p] is the direct sum of the V(α_j) ⊗ σ(τ), each τ once; as in GK.3/projective-lift-freeness, BHHMS (71)–(72) and the domain property give S = R∞/∩_τ p_τ.

By GK.4/adjoint-type-lattices each M∞(V(α_j) ⊗ σ(τ)°)[1/p] is free of rank r over R∞^{(2,−1)_j,τ}[1/p], so M∞(R′_{2,j})[1/p] is locally free of rank r over S[1/p]; hence ker(f)[1/p] = 0 and, S having no p-torsion, ker(f) = 0.

nodes.title: L_j and N_j agree modulo the third radical
nodes.statement: For j ∈ {0, …, f − 1} the surjection L_j ↠ N_j of GK.4/glued-lattices (formed with τ₀) induces an isomorphism (L_j/pL_j)/rad³_K(L_j/pL_j) ≅ (N_j/pN_j)/rad³_K(N_j/pN_j).
hypotheses: rad^i_K denotes the i-th power of the radical of finite-dimensional K-representations over 𝔽; taking rad^i preserves surjections (Alperin, Local representation theory, §1 Proposition 4).
proofSteps: The reductions fit into a commutative diagram of short exact sequences 0 → R_{2,j}/p → L_j/p → L_{j−1}/p → 0 and 0 → T_{2,j}/p → N_j/p → L_{j−1}/p → 0, with left vertical map γ identified with F(α_j) ⊗ (P̃/p ↠ σ(τ₀)°/p), surjective; so L_j/p ↠ N_j/p (the map β).

For a quotient M of (Proj_{K/Z₁}σ_v)/𝔪²_{K₁} admitting P as a quotient, M/rad^i(M) ≅ P/rad^i(P) for i = 1, 2 (MP.5/first-order-weight-hulls); L_j/p, N_j/p and L_{j−1}/p are such quotients (GK.4/glued-lattices), so ker β = ker rad²(β), and the same diagram for rad² gives ker rad²(β) = ker γ.
It remains that ker γ ⊆ rad_K(R_{2,j}/pR_{2,j}), i.e. that γ is an isomorphism on cosocles, which is the dual of the proof of BHHMS Lemma 6.3.8 (MP.6/adjoint-tensor).

acceptance: The isomorphism is modulo rad³ of the reductions modulo p, not of the lattices.

nodes.title: Generation of M∞(L_j) and of M∞(N_j)
nodes.statement: For j ∈ {0, …, f − 1}, M∞(L_j) is generated by r elements over R∞ if and only if M∞(N_j) is.
hypotheses: N_j formed with τ₀; π the weighted representation, with π^{K₁} ≅ D₀(r̄_v^∨)^{⊕r} (GK.3/projective-lift-freeness).
proofSteps: By GK.1/patched-fibre-identity, generation by r elements is equivalent to dim_𝔽 Hom_K(L_j, π) = r (resp. Hom_K(N_j, π)); since N_j is a quotient of L_j the forward implication is clear.

Conversely, suppose dim Hom_K(L_j, π) > r; since dim Hom_K(σ_v, π) = r there is h : L_j → π not factoring through cosoc L_j = σ_v; choose one with [Im h : σ_v] minimal and put Q = Im h. Minimality and relative projectivity (MP.9/relative-projectivity, applicable because L_j/p is a quotient of L_{f−1}/p (GK.4/glued-lattices), which is (Proj_{K/Z₁}σ_v)/𝔪²_{K₁} by MP.8/projective-truncation for the 8-deep σ_v) force [Q/soc_K Q : σ_v] = 1.

From π^{K₁} = D₀(r̄_v^∨)^{⊕r}, soc_K Q consists of modular weights, so Q satisfies (a)–(b) of GK.4/loewy-length-three; then rad_K(Q) ⊆ π^{K₁}, and rad_K Q/soc_K Q embeds in π^{K₁}/soc_K π, giving (c)–(d); hence Q has Loewy length ≤ 3.

By GK.4/comparison-lattice-truncation h factors through N_j, contradicting the hypothesis on N_j. (In the source this step reads dim Hom_K(σ_v, π) = f; the correct value is r, recorded as a source finding.)

nodes.title: Freeness of the patched glued lattices (BHHMS Theorem 1.8)
nodes.statement: For j ∈ {−1, …, f − 1}, M∞(L_j) is free of rank r over R∞/∩_{λ,τ} p_{λ,τ}, where p_{λ,τ} = ker(R∞ ↠ R∞^{λ,τ}), τ runs over the tame inertial types with σ_v ∈ JH(σ(τ)), and λ = (λ_{j′})_{0≤j′<f} over the labelled weights with λ_{j′} ∈ {(1, 0), (2, −1)} for j′ ≤ j and λ_{j′} = (1, 0) for j′ > j. In particular the rank does not depend on j or on σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨).
hypotheses: Generic global datum (p > 23); σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨).

The presentation of the multi-type ring R_{r̄_v^∨}^{≤(3,0),σ_v} (BHHMS Proposition 4.3.1), its prime ideals (Lemma 4.3.2) and the membership p ∈ q₁^{(j),(2,1)} ∩ q₂^{(j),(2,1)} + p₂^{(j),(3,0)} (Proposition 4.3.3) are the recorded multi-type gap, owned by LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartII; all R∞^{λ,τ} are domains by the single-type gap.
proofSteps: Use the twist/reindexing of BHHMS proof of Theorem 8.3.9: after twisting deformations by ε the labelled weights are (2, 1) and (3, 0), the determinant is ε³ψ_v^{−1}, and the type-index condition is σ_v ⊗ (N_{k/𝔽_p} ∘ det^{−1}) ∈ JH(σ(τ)) in that proof’s reindexed notation. Keep this negative norm twist in the type-to-prime bijection as well (the positive sign in its displayed ι on p. 102 is inconsistent with the defining index set). Induct on j; j = −1 is GK.3/projective-lift-freeness.

Generation of M∞(N_j): M∞(N_j) = M∞(L_{j−1}) ×_{M∞(Y_j)} M∞(T′_{2,j}) by exactness, the three modules are free of rank r over their supports (induction, GK.4/adjoint-type-lattices), so by GK.2/fibre-product-freeness it suffices that Ann(M∞(Y_j)) ⊆ Ann(M∞(L_{j−1})) + Ann(M∞(T′_{2,j})); as Ann(M∞(Y_j)) = (p) + Ann(M∞(T′_{2,j})) (GK.4/adjoint-type-lattices), it suffices that p ∈ Ann(M∞(L_{j−1})) + Ann(M∞(T′_{2,j})).

Use the multi-type ring R∞^{≤(3,0),σ_v} = R∞/∩_{λ,τ}p_{λ,τ} ≅ S⟦X₁, …, X_h⟧ with S an explicit completed tensor product of rings S^{(j)} modulo an ideal, the explicit primes p_k^λ = Σ_j p_{k_j}^{(j),λ_j} indexed by k ∈ {1, 2}^f via a bijection with the types, and τ₀ ↔ k = (2, …, 2). Then Ann(M∞(T′_{2,j})) = p₂^{λ(j)} and Ann(M∞(L_{j−1})) ⊇ q₁^{(j),(2,1)} ∩ q₂^{(j),(2,1)}, so the needed membership is p ∈ q₁^{(j),(2,1)} ∩ q₂^{(j),(2,1)} + p₂^{(j),(3,0)}, which is BHHMS Proposition 4.3.3.

nodes.title: Multiplicity one for the first-order projective envelope (BHHMS Theorem 8.3.11)
nodes.statement: M∞(R) is free of rank r over R∞/∩_{λ,τ} p_{λ,τ}, with τ over the tame types with σ_v ∈ JH(σ(τ)) and λ_j ∈ {(1, 0), (2, −1)} for every j, and dim_𝔽 M∞(R)/𝔪∞ = r. nodes.title: Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of the weighted representation (BHHMS Theorem 1.10)
nodes.statement: For a generic global datum and the weighted representation π of GK.0/infinite-level-representation, dim_{GL₂(F_v)}(π) = f = [F_v : ℚ_p].
hypotheses: dim_{GL₂(F_v)} is the dimension of ModpRepresentationsOfGL2OverLocalFields MP.4/gk-dimension: 3f minus the grade of π^∨ over 𝔽⟦K₁/Z₁⟧.
proofSteps: Upper bound: verify the three hypotheses of MP.7/local-gk-bound for ρ = r̄_v^∨. (i) JH(soc_K π) = W(r̄_v^∨) by the weight theorem (GK.0/bdj-weight-theorem). (ii) [π[𝔪²_{K₁}] : σ_v] = [soc_K π : σ_v] for σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨) by GK.4/second-truncation-multiplicity in its Hom form. (iii) JH(π^{I₁}) = JH(D₁(r̄_v^∨)): since K₁ ⊆ I₁, π^{I₁} = (π^{K₁})^{I₁} = (D₀(r̄_v^∨)^{⊕r})^{I₁} = D₁(r̄_v^∨)^{⊕r} by GK.3/projective-lift-freeness and MP.3/diamond-socle (BHHMS argue instead with Breuil's Lemma 9.2 and Breuil–Paškūnas Lemma 14.1); MP.7/diamond-connected (D₁ of a tame 6-deep ρ is connected) and MP.7/connected-characters turn (iii) into the connectedness hypothesis. Lower bound: let M∞ be the big patched module (GK.1/big-patched-module). By GK.2/iwasawa-grade-and-power-series (2) for A = R∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧ and MP.4/dimension-comparisons, j_{R∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧}(M∞) ≥ j_{𝔽⟦K₁/Z₁⟧}(M∞/𝔪∞) = 3f − dim π (BHHMS (80)).

M∞ is finite free over S∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧, so its grade there is 0 and its dimension is dim S∞ + dim K₁/Z₁; by GK.2/iwasawa-grade-and-power-series (3) its dimension over R∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧ is the same, so j_{R∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧}(M∞) = dim R∞ − dim S∞ = 2f (GK.1/patched-deformation-ring; BHHMS (81)).
Combining, 2f ≥ 3f − dim π, so dim π ≥ f.
