nodes.title: Structure of π[𝔪²_{K₁}] (BHHMS Theorem 1.9)
nodes.statement: For the weighted π there is r ≥ 1 with π[𝔪²_{K₁}] ≅ (⊕_{σ_v∈W(r̄_v^∨)} D̃_{σ_v})^{⊕r} as K-representations, where D̃_{σ_v} is the largest subrepresentation of (Inj_{K/Z₁}σ_v)[𝔪²_{K₁}] containing σ_v with multiplicity one (as its socle) and no other weight of W(r̄_v^∨). Every irreducible constituent of π[𝔪²_{K₁}] occurs with multiplicity r.
hypotheses: 𝔪_{K₁} is the maximal ideal of 𝔽⟦K₁/Z₁⟧ and π[𝔪²_{K₁}] the subspace killed by its square.
D̃_{σ_v} is the summand V_{σ_v} of MP.6/socle-enlargement for the tame representation r̄_v^∨ (BHHMS Corollary 6.3.13).
proofSteps: M∞ is finite projective over S∞⟦K⟧_Z (GK.1/big-patched-module), so M∞/(p, x₁, …) is finite projective over 𝔽⟦K⟧_Z; since Hom(M∞/(p, x), σ_v^∨)^∨ = M∞(σ_v)/(p, x) is nonzero exactly for σ_v ∈ W(r̄_v^∨), M∞/(p, x) ≅ ⊕_{σ_v}(Proj_{K/Z₁}σ_v^∨)^{m_{σ_v}} with m_{σ_v} ≥ r.
By the defining property of D̃_{σ_v}, restriction gives Hom(M∞/(p, x), D̃_{σ_v}^∨) ≅ Hom(M∞/(p, x), σ_v^∨); taking 𝔪∞-torsion and M∞/𝔪∞ ≅ π^∨ gives Hom_K(D̃_{σ_v}, π) ≅ Hom_K(σ_v, soc_K π).

As soc_K π = (⊕σ_v)^{⊕r} (GK.3/weight-and-type-freeness), (⊕D̃_{σ_v})^{⊕r} ⊆ π[𝔪²_{K₁}]; it cannot be larger by MP.6/socle-enlargement and GK.4/second-truncation-multiplicity; multiplicities by the constituent description of MP.6/socle-enlargement.

nodes.title: The big patched module is faithfully flat over R∞
nodes.statement: The big patched module M∞ is a faithfully flat R∞-module.
hypotheses: Generic global datum; M∞ as in GK.1/big-patched-module, finite free over S∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧.
proofSteps: M∞ is free of finite rank over A = S∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧, hence Cohen–Macaulay over A; by GK.2/iwasawa-cohen-macaulay-transfer it is Cohen–Macaulay over B = R∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧ (R∞ is a power series ring over W(𝔽) by GK.1/patched-deformation-ring, so B is an Iwasawa algebra with power-series coefficients).
By GK.5/patched-gk-dimension and the computations (80)–(81) there, j_B(M∞) = 2f = j_{𝔽⟦K₁/Z₁⟧}(M∞/𝔪∞).
GK.2/iwasawa-miracle-flatness gives flatness over R∞; M∞/𝔪∞ ≅ π^∨ ≠ 0 and R∞ is local, so M∞ is faithfully flat.

nodes.title: Nonzero Banach lifts of π (BHHMS Theorem 1.3)
nodes.statement: Let x : R∞ → O′ be a homomorphism of local W(𝔽)-algebras, O′ the integers of a finite extension E′ of E = W(𝔽)[1/p], with residue field 𝔽′. Then V(x) = Hom^{cont}_{O′}(M∞ ⊗_{R∞,x} O′, E′) is a nonzero admissible unitary Banach representation of GL₂(F_v) over E′, with GL₂(F_v)-invariant unit ball Hom^{cont}_{O′}(M∞ ⊗_{R∞,x} O′, O′) whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal of O′ is π ⊗_𝔽 𝔽′.
hypotheses: x induces a lift ρ_x : G_{F_v} → GL₂(E′) of r̄_v^∨ (up to the duality convention); V(x) is the candidate of CEGGPS for the p-adic Langlands correspondence, now known to be nonzero.
proofSteps: Admissibility and unitarity: let x̄ : R∞ → 𝔽′ be x followed by residue reduction. The kernel of x̄ on S∞ is open; the kernel of x itself need not be open. The finite generation of M∞ over S∞⟦K⟧ and topological Nakayama imply finite generation of M∞ ⊗_{R∞,x} O′ over O′⟦K⟧, using its finite residual module. CEGGPS Proposition 2.13 and the duality of LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.6 then give an admissible unitary Banach representation.

Nonvanishing: M∞ is flat over R∞ (GK.5/patched-faithful-flatness), so M∞ ⊗_{R∞,x} O′ is flat over O′, that is torsion free; it is nonzero since its reduction is π^∨ ⊗ 𝔽′ ≠ 0; Schikhof duality (Schneider–Teitelbaum, Theorem 1.2) then gives V(x) ≠ 0.
The unit ball reduces to the dual of M∞ ⊗_{R∞} 𝔽′ = (M∞/𝔪∞) ⊗ 𝔽′ ≅ π^∨ ⊗ 𝔽′, i.e. to π ⊗ 𝔽′.

nodes.title: Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of mod p cohomology of Shimura curves (BHHMS Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement: Let a generic global datum be given (with S = S_D ∪ S_r) and let V^v = ∏_{w∉S_D∪S_r}(O_D)_w^× · ∏_{w∈(S_D∪S_r)∖{v}} V_w ⊆ ∏_{w≠v}(O_D)_w^× be a compact open subgroup with V_w ⊆ 1 + pM₂(O_{F_w}) for w ∈ S_p ∖ {v}, such that π ≠ 0, where π = colim_{V_v} Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹_ét(X_{V^vV_v} ×_F F̄, 𝔽)) in the indefinite case and π = colim_{V_v} S(V^vV_v, 𝔽)[𝔪] in the definite case. Then dim_{GL₂(F_v)}(π) = [F_v : ℚ_p]. Without the condition V_w ⊆ 1 + pM₂(O_{F_w}) at w ∈ S_p ∖ {v} one still has dim_{GL₂(F_v)}(π) ≤ [F_v : ℚ_p]; and the equality holds for V^v = ∏_{w∉S}(O_D)_w^× ∏_{w∈S∖{v}}V_w for any finite S ⊇ S_D ∪ S_r, with the same nonvanishing and pro-p conditions at the other places above p, such that the framed deformation ring of r̄_w is formally smooth for w ∈ S ∖ S_p.
hypotheses: The hypotheses on r̄: absolutely irreducible on G_{F(ζ_p)}, generic at the places above p other than v, of the stated semisimple inertial shape at v (so p > 23), formally smooth local rings at the bad places away from p.
In the definite case 𝔪 is the ideal of BHHMS Remark 8.1.3(ii) for S large; the eigenspace does not depend on S (BDJ10 Lemma 4.6(a)).
proofSteps: Upper bound: the dimension of a subrepresentation is at most that of the space, so shrink V^v: take V_{w₁} unipotent upper triangular modulo w₁ and V_w ⊆ 1 + pM₂(O_{F_w}) normal at w ∈ S_p ∖ {v}; then S = S_D ∪ S_r and U = ∏U_w (U_w = V_w off S_p, U_w = GL₂(O_{F_w}) on S_p) satisfy GK.0/generic-global-datum.

Dévissage (BHHMS (83)): π ≅ colim Hom_{U^v/V^v}(⊗_w(Ind_{V_w}^{GL₂(O_{F_w})}1)_Z, Hom_{G_F}(r̄, H¹)); filtering the induced representations by Serre weights and using that H¹_𝔪 is injective over U^v/V^v (GK.0/non-eisenstein-freeness), and that the dimension of an extension is the maximum and that of a subrepresentation at most that of the whole (grades in short exact sequences, GK.2/iwasawa-cohen-macaulay), dim π is the maximum over weight tuples of the dimensions of the weighted π, which are f or zero by GK.5/patched-gk-dimension and GK.0/bdj-weight-theorem; so dim π ≤ f, with equality as soon as one modular tuple occurs, which π ≠ 0 forces.

For the lower bound at the original levels V_w ⊆ K₁,w, enlarge those levels to K₁,w. The original nonzero smooth representation of the compact pro-p group ∏ K₁,w has nonzero invariant vectors; the weight theorem then provides a modular weight tuple whose weighted π embeds at these enlarged levels and has dimension f by GK.5/patched-gk-dimension. The inclusion from enlarged-level cohomology into the original smaller-level space gives dimension at least f. Remove the auxiliary level at w₁ with GK.0/ihara-at-auxiliary-place: its doubling does not change dimension. Together with the upper bound this gives equality at the original level; shrinking to K₁,w would reverse the required inclusion.
The variant with a larger S (BHHMS Remark 8.4.7) is the same argument with S in place of S_D ∪ S_r.

nodes.title: Completed cohomology at the r̄-part and the big Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Assume p is inert in F (so S_p = {v}) and let V^v = ∏_{w≠v}U_w. For compact open V_v ⊆ 1 + pM₂(O_{F_v}) and n ≥ 1 let H¹_ét(X_{V^vV_v} ×_F F̄, W(𝔽)/pⁿ)^{ψ^{−1}} (definite: S(V^vV_v, W(𝔽)/pⁿ)^{ψ^{−1}}) be the ψ^{−1}-isotypic part for the centre (𝔸_F^∞)^×, ψ^{−1} viewed as a character of (𝔸_F^∞)^× by the global Artin map sending uniformizers to geometric Frobenius; let T(V^vV_v, W(𝔽)/pⁿ)^{ψ^{−1}} be the W(𝔽)-subalgebra of its endomorphisms generated by the T_w, S_w for w ∉ S ∪ {w₁}, and T(…)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}} its localisation at 𝔪. The big Hecke algebra is T̂(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}} = lim_{n,V_v} T(V^vV_v, W(𝔽)/pⁿ)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}}, and the localized completed cohomology is Ĥ¹(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}} = lim_n colim_{V_v} (H¹(…, W(𝔽)/pⁿ)^{ψ^{−1}} ⊗_{T(…)} T(…)_{r̄}) (definite: Ŝ(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}}), whose W(𝔽)-dual Hom_{W(𝔽)}(Ĥ¹(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}}, W(𝔽)) is a T̂(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}}-module. R^ψ_{r̄,S∪{w₁}} is the universal deformation ring of r̄ for deformations unramified outside S ∪ {w₁} with ψ = ε det.
hypotheses: p inert in F is assumed in BHHMS §8.5; for other p the corresponding statement is expected but not proved there (BHHMS Remark 8.5.2).
proofSteps: Specialise the completed cohomology and completed Hecke algebra of CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.8 (completed-hecke-algebra, completed-residual-localisation) to the quaternionic Shimura-curve tower of HMV R18.4/finite-cohomology with level varying at v, with the ψ^{−1}-isotypic projection of the centre.

CC.8 defines finite Hecke images on the derived cohomology complexes. After the non-Eisenstein localisation, H⁰ and H² vanish, so the indefinite complex is concentrated in degree 1 and is its H¹ shifted; in the definite case it is concentrated in degree 0. Thus those derived Hecke images agree with the images on the cohomology modules used here, compatibly through the tower. This identifies the imported construction rather than silently changing its carrier.

The deformation ring is GlobalGaloisDeformations' universal deformation ring with fixed determinant (R04.1/fixed-determinant-functors, R04.3/global-framed-ring); the map R^ψ_{r̄,S∪{w₁}} → T̂ is the inverse limit of the finite-level maps given by the Galois representations on localized Hecke algebras (HMV R18.4/early-quaternionic-galois-hecke-support), sending traces of Frobenius to Hecke operators; CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.3/deformation-to-hecke-surjection is the analogue for the modular tower.

nodes.title: Big R = big T and flatness of completed cohomology (BHHMS Theorem 1.2)
nodes.statement: Assume p inert in F. In the sequence of surjections R∞ ⊗_{S∞} W(𝔽) = R∞/(x₁, …, x_{4|S|+q−1}) ↠ R^ψ_{r̄,S∪{w₁}} ↠ T̂(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}} all maps are isomorphisms; Hom_{W(𝔽)}(Ĥ¹(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}}, W(𝔽)) (resp. the dual of Ŝ(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}}) is a faithfully flat T̂(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}}-module; and T̂(V^v)_{r̄}^{ψ^{−1}} is a complete intersection.
hypotheses: Generic global datum with p inert in F; V_{w₁} sufficiently small at the chosen auxiliary place.
proofSteps: By GK.1/big-patched-module, M∞/(x₁, …) is the dual of the localized completed cohomology, compatibly with the surjections; it is faithfully flat over R∞/(x₁, …) by base change of GK.5/patched-faithful-flatness.
A faithfully flat module is faithful, so the composite R∞/(x) ↠ R^ψ ↠ T̂ → End_{W(𝔽)}(dual of Ĥ¹) is injective; hence all maps are isomorphisms, and the dual of Ĥ¹ is faithfully flat over T̂.

M∞ is faithfully flat over R∞ and over S∞ (finite free over S∞⟦K₁/Z₁⟧), so R∞ is faithfully flat over S∞; thus the regular sequence (x₁, …) of S∞ is R∞-regular and T̂ ≅ R∞/(x₁, …) is a power series ring over W(𝔽) modulo a regular sequence, a complete intersection (BHHMS reproduce Gee–Newton Proposition 4.3.1 in this setting).

gaps.title: The multi-type deformation ring R^{≤(3,0),σ_v} and the membership of p
gaps.detail: For a generic residual representation ρ̄ and a modular indexing weight σ as in BHHMS §4.3: Proposition 4.3.1, pp. 34–35, gives the stabilised presentation R_{ρ̄}^{≤(3,0),σ}⟦X₁, …, X_{2f}⟧ ≅ S⟦Y₁, …, Y₄⟧, with S = (⊗̂_j S^{(j)})/J explicit. After the relabelling 3 → 1 used in §8.3, Lemma 4.3.2, p. 39, gives q_1^{(j),(2,1)}, q_2^{(j),(2,1)}, and Proposition 4.3.3, pp. 39–40, gives p ∈ q_1^{(j),(2,1)} ∩ q_2^{(j),(2,1)} + p_2^{(j),(3,0)}. For the patched ring, increasing q and applying Hamann cancellation gives a presentation S⟦X₁, …, X_h⟧ with h ≥ 1; no unstabilised presentation of the bare local ring is asserted. Apply the residual and weight twists as in Theorem 8.3.9, pp. 101–102. Matched the subset recipes, antisymmetry and exceptional extension-class conditions. The comparison is W(ρ) = D_EGS(ρ^∨); the p = 5 boundary has three weights. Checked against BDJ10 §§3.1–3.2, pp. 18–26; EGS15 §2.1, pp. 10–11.

Checked the centre quotient and ψ⁻¹, the contravariance of S and covariance of its dual M, and the augmentation counterexample before non-Eisenstein localisation. Checked against EGS15 §6.2, pp. 34–35; BHHMS23 Remark 8.1.3 and (64), pp. 88–89.

The perfect localized complex gives a projective and injective module for any finite deck group. Freeness needs a p-group; a prime-to-p direct summand need not be free. Checked against BHHMS23 (64), p. 89 and Corollary 8.4.6(i), p. 107; EGS15 §6.2, p. 35.

Checked the infinite-level multiplicity carrier, fixed away-from-v weights, admissibility and ψ⁻¹ central character. Twisting r̄ by χ twists π by χ⁻¹ composed with determinant. Checked against BHHMS23 (65)–(68), pp. 89–90; DL21 §6.2, pp. 54–55.

Checked the global irreducibility and small-prime conditions and the unramified weight identification. Nonvanishing for precisely the modular weights still depends on the explicit Breuil–Mézard gap. Checked against GK14 Theorem B, p. 3, Corollary 5.4.5, p. 33 and Corollaries 5.5.4, 5.5.7, pp. 34–36.

The auxiliary-place eigenvalue exclusions make the degeneracy Gram determinant a unit. Localized non-Eisenstein control supplies the doubling, so GK dimension is unchanged. Checked against BHHMS23 Corollary 8.4.6(ii), p. 107; EGS15 §6.2, p. 35.

Read Hamann directly and corrected the variable count: A[[x]] ≅ B[[x]] with B ≅ W[[n]] gives A ≅ W[[n]], whereas A[[x]] ≅ W[[n]] gives n−1 variables. Checked against HAM75 Theorem 4, printed p. 155; BHHMS23 Lemma 8.1.2, p. 88.

Checked the dimensions of R∞ and S∞. The one-variable fixed/unfixed determinant comparison concerns fixed-Hodge/inertial-type loci; unrestricted local determinant characters have f+1 parameters. Checked against BHHMS23 (63), pp. 88–89; GK14 Remark 5.2.2, p. 26.

Checked the type and Hodge quotient conventions and domain assumptions. A non-Barsotti–Tate quotient example requires a nonzero characteristic-zero point with different Hodge–Tate weights. Checked against BHHMS23 (69), pp. 90–91; EGS15 Theorems 7.1.1–7.2.1, pp. 42–43.

Checked exactness, maximal Cohen–Macaulay conditions on the weight and type supports, covariant variance, reduction compatibility and the separate rank-one minimality condition. Checked against EGS15 Definitions 6.1.1, 6.1.3 and Lemma 6.1.4, pp. 32–34.

The augmentation gives the module comparison and a ring surjection to the locally constrained global ring. An isomorphism or the unrestricted global ring is not supplied at this stage. Checked against EGS15 §§6.2–6.4, pp. 34–37; GK14 §5.4.1, pp. 30–31; BHHMS23 (62)–(64), pp. 88–89.

Checked the Pontryagin dual of Hom at the patched fibre and exactness. For an integral lattice, the relevant Jordan–Hölder constituents are those of σ/pσ, with Nakayama used afterwards. Checked against BHHMS23 (64)–(68), pp. 89–90.

Checked the compact-module GL₂ action and S∞[[K₁/Z₁]] freeness. No finiteness over R∞ is asserted; the completed-cohomology fibre needs p inert. Checked against DL21 Theorem 6.2 and §6.2, pp. 53–55; BHHMS23 Theorem 8.4.1(ii), p. 104 and (84), p. 108.

Checked Ext grade, the convention for the zero module, depth and canonical dimension. Auslander regularity and the local GK carrier remain imports, rather than duplicate targets. Checked against GN22 Definitions A.2, A.5, Proposition A.4 and Lemmas A.7–A.9, pp. 42–44.

Checked r ≥ 1, the annihilator-quotient isomorphism and generation by r elements. The kernel argument needs surjective endomorphisms of finite modules to be injective; no Noetherian hypothesis is smuggled in. Checked against BHHMS23 Lemma 8.2.1, pp. 90–91; Stacks Tag 05G8.

Checked both surjections, nonzero finite free modules of a common rank over their supports, the intersection annihilator and the equivalent sum-ideal criterion. Bases can be aligned over the local quotient. Checked against BHHMS23 Lemma 8.3.8, p. 101.

Checked each grade identity and inequality with its finiteness hypotheses over the smaller and larger algebras; the central power-series and regular-sequence cases have different shifts. Checked against GN22 Proposition A.13 and Lemmas A.15–A.19, pp. 45–47.

Checked central regular-sequence grade transfer, finite projective dimension and purity. The conclusion transfers Cohen–Macaulayness without assuming the flatness that the next target will prove. Checked against GN22 Lemmas A.21–A.28 and Corollary A.29, pp. 47–49.

Checked Noetherian local base, central ideal, depth and grade bounds. The lifting argument requires adic separation of every I tensor M; finiteness over the larger Noetherian algebra supplies it. Checked against GN22 Proposition A.30, pp. 49–50; Stacks Tags 00MK and 090V.

Checked that finite S∞-freeness and the support dimension force depth to equal dimension for finite-length coefficients; deeper rings and modules remain README targets. Checked against BHHMS23 Lemma 8.2.2, p. 91.

Checked the weight-isolating types, the lattice comparisons and propagation of a single positive rank r across all modular weights and tame types. Local ring inputs are explicitly gaps. Checked against BHHMS23 Proposition 8.2.3, pp. 91–92; EGS15 Proposition 10.1.11 and proof, pp. 63–65.

Checked the reduced support, maximal Cohen–Macaulay assertion and regular characteristic-zero loci. The imported potential-diagonalisability argument supplies local freeness without forcing r = 1. Checked against BHHMS23 Corollary 8.2.4 and Remark 8.2.5, pp. 92–93; CEGGPS16 Lemmas 4.17–4.18, pp. 62–66.

Separated the upper embedding into D₀^r from its reverse. Breuil’s localized extension argument gives the reverse embedding using essential socle and absence of modular constituents in the quotient; neither the GK bound nor GK.4 is used. Checked against BHHMS23 Proposition 8.2.6, pp. 93–94; LMS22 Lemma 4.5 and Proposition 4.6, pp. 14–15; BRE14 Lemma 9.2, pp. 54–55.

Checked the integral pullbacks defining L_j and N_j, the maps to P, the comparison lattices and the unique τ₀ with all modular constituents. The endpoint lattice R is imported from MP.8. Checked against BHHMS23 §8.3, pp. 95, 98–99 and 101.

Checked all four distinct conditions on the quotient and its socle, the K₁-invariance statement and the extra hypotheses for Loewy length at most three. None is silently implied by a shared socle. Checked against BHHMS23 Lemma 8.3.1, pp. 94–95.

Checked the mod-radical relations in the projective presentation and the minimal-generator count. The patched multiplicity is the common r, not an assumed multiplicity one. Checked against BHHMS23 Lemma 8.3.2, pp. 95–96; LE19 Lemma 4.5, p. 16.

Checked the characteristic-zero type decomposition, the nonmodular constituents killed by exact patching and the special-fibre comparison M∞(T′/p) ≅ M∞(Y). Checked against BHHMS23 Proposition 8.3.3, pp. 96–98 and Lemma 8.3.5, p. 99.

Checked the support prime intersection, the adjoint-type lattice decomposition and the use of the extension freeness criterion. Its generation prerequisite is the preceding target, not the later glued-lattice theorem. Checked against BHHMS23 Theorem 8.3.4, p. 98.

Checked the comparison of L_j and N_j modulo the third radical and its relative-projectivity input from MP.9. It identifies this truncation, not the whole lattices. Checked against BHHMS23 Lemma 8.3.6, pp. 99–100.

Checked the contradiction via a Loewy-length-three quotient, relative projectivity and the repaired D₀ identification. The needed Hom dimension is r; the source’s occurrence of f is recorded as E1. Checked against BHHMS23 Proposition 8.3.7, pp. 100–101.

Checked the full norm-determinant twist, prime relabelling and fibre-product induction. Only a stabilized bare-local-ring presentation is imported; increasing q and cancellation give the patched power-series presentation. Checked against BHHMS23 Theorem 8.3.9, pp. 101–103 and Proposition 4.3.1, pp. 34–38.

Checked the endpoint L_{f−1}, its imported projective-envelope reduction and the fibre multiplicity isomorphism. The isomorphism is after quotienting by 𝔪∞ and does not assert equality before the fibre. Checked against BHHMS23 Corollary 8.3.10, Theorem 8.3.11 and Remark 8.3.12, p. 103.

Checked all three hypotheses of the imported local GK bound, including second-truncation multiplicity, and the independent lower bound from the S∞-free big module and grade inequalities. Checked against BHHMS23 Theorem 8.4.1, pp. 104–105.

Checked the enlarged socle construction and the multiplicities furnished by the second-truncation theorem. The structural identification uses MP.6 and does not assume faithful flatness. Checked against BHHMS23 Theorem 8.4.2, p. 105.

Checked the Cohen–Macaulay transfer and grade 2f, the miracle-flatness hypotheses and nonzero residual fibre for faithfulness. Finiteness is over the larger Iwasawa algebra. Checked against BHHMS23 Theorem 8.4.3, pp. 105–106; GN22 Corollary A.29 and Proposition A.30, pp. 49–50.

Checked the integral specialization, nonzero residual fibre and the bounded dual Banach construction. Topological Nakayama uses the open residual kernel of x̄, not the kernel of the characteristic-zero point. Checked against BHHMS23 Corollary 8.4.4, p. 106; CEGGPS16 Proposition 2.13 and Remark 2.14, p. 34.

Checked finite-level dévissage and auxiliary-place doubling. For the lower bound, enlarge the other pro-p levels to K₁ and take nonzero invariants; the larger-S variant retains nonvanishing and level hypotheses. Checked against BHHMS23 Corollary 8.4.6, pp. 106–107 and Remark 8.4.7, p. 108.

Checked the inverse-limit central-character cohomology and Hecke carrier. Non-Eisenstein H⁰ and H² vanishing identifies the imported derived Hecke image with the H¹-image definition used here. Checked against BHHMS23 §8.5, pp. 108–109; CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.8.

Checked p inert, the completed-cohomology fibre and the chain of surjections. Faithful flatness kills its kernels and descends the regular patching sequence, giving the complete intersection conclusion. Checked against BHHMS23 Corollary 8.5.1, p. 109; GN22 Proposition 4.3.1, pp. 31–32.
